## 2026-06-11 DA/RBC retained-summary payload evidence hardening

- Hardened pending-block `rbc_deliver` validation priority so a retained
  status-only delivered summary cannot elevate priority unless the pending
  block's local payload bytes hash to the advertised payload hash. Live RBC
  sessions now use both complete byte-verified chunk evidence and the same
  pending-local-body hash binding before they can elevate `rbc_deliver`
  priority.
- Applied the same boundary to missing-QC frontier cleanup through the shared
  delivered-RBC helper: a retained delivered summary remains diagnostic when
  the local pending body hashes differently, but it no longer makes the repair
  path treat the payload as available.
- Tightened retained READY-quorum summaries on the same path. Status-only READY
  counters now need the pending block's local payload bytes and the retained
  summary payload hash to match the advertised payload before they can elevate
  validation priority or preserve missing-QC repair availability.
- Tightened live READY-quorum validation priority to the same payload boundary:
  a live session's READY count now only contributes when the pending local body
  hashes to the advertised payload hash and the live RBC session advertises that
  same payload hash.
- Pinned pending-block READY-quorum validation priority to the protocol READY
  quorum even when the test-only `force_deliver_quorum_one` debug shortcut
  lowers local emission helpers. Live sessions and retained status summaries now
  both require protocol quorum before they can schedule `rbc_ready_quorum`
  priority.
- Pinned stale-pending DA availability reschedule gates to the protocol READY
  quorum as well. Complete delivered RBC chunks with only the debug-lowered
  one-READY threshold still count as availability-incomplete until receiver-side
  protocol quorum is present or the configured availability timeout expires.
- Hardened DA availability proofing for live RBC fallback payloads: complete
  chunk bytes now need matching block-header height/view/hash metadata and a
  leader signature that verifies against the resolved session roster before
  they can satisfy production `payload_available_for_da` or suppress
  missing-block repair as authoritative payload evidence. Summary-only status
  remains diagnostic-only and malformed or forged-signature live sessions no
  longer bypass the missing-local-data gate. The old map-based byte predicate is
  now test-only, keeping production callers on the actor-level roster-verified
  path.
- Bound local RBC READY and DELIVER signing to the same INIT metadata invariant:
  helpers that build local signatures now reject sessions without matching
  block-header height/view/hash metadata or a leader signature that verifies
  against the session roster for the progress height/view. READY rebroadcast
  bundles remain limited to already-recorded peer signatures, while session-only
  rebroadcast activity now also rejects key/header height drift.
- Decoupled inbound READY relay from the `force_deliver_quorum_one` debug
  shortcut. A node that sees enough external READY evidence to relay its local
  READY now uses the protocol READY relay threshold even when debug settings
  lower local DELIVER emission, so under-quorum DELIVER handling cannot stall
  READY relay until the full roster signs.
- Decoupled READY propagation repair and cached-slot liveness from the same
  debug shortcut. Broad READY rebroadcast suppression, targeted missing-READY
  payload/body rescue, and cached-slot timeout pressure now use receiver-side
  protocol quorum, so a one-READY debug DELIVER threshold cannot suppress READY
  fanout, unlock payload/body rescue, or release reduced timeout pressure early.
- Removed stale commit quorum-bypass plumbing from the finalize/commit-worker
  path. Commit QC materialization now reads as an unconditional "derive a QC if
  none is cached" step, and the worker/inflight records no longer carry a
  permanently-false bypass bit that could obscure production quorum
  requirements.
- Simplified RBC progress-stage synchronization so it no longer accepts an
  unused READY-quorum argument. Receiver-side protocol quorum enforcement
  remains centralized in DELIVER acceptance, while progress sync now only tracks
  verified payload knowledge, local READY emission, and accepted DELIVER state.
- Removed an unreachable READY-quorum tail from near-tip RBC payload
  backpressure exemption. `allows_payload_recovery()` already guarantees a
  non-empty session with missing local chunks, so the helper now exposes the
  intended repair exemption directly without consulting a debug-aware quorum
  helper in dead code.
- Added an adversarial local-DELIVER bypass regression: the
  post-local-READY fast path may only emit early DELIVER for locally
  authoritative payloads. Complete peer-only RBC bytes with one local READY now
  have direct coverage proving they stay deferred until protocol READY quorum
  instead of using the local-authority shortcut.
- Pinned inbound READY commit-pipeline wakeups to protocol READY quorum as
  well. When `force_deliver_quorum_one` lowers local helper thresholds, a
  complete delivered session plus one accepted READY no longer records
  `BlockAvailable` or wakes the commit pipeline until the receiver observes
  protocol quorum.
- Extended that key/header/signature binding to cached RBC INIT and payload
  bundle rebuilds. `rebuild_rbc_init(...)` and `rbc_payload_bundle(...)` now
  refuse sessions whose cached block header is validly signed by the
  roster-derived leader but belongs to a different block hash, height, or view
  than the session key.
- Hardened late missing-BlockCreated repair targeting so cached RBC
  leader-signature indices only influence preferred signer selection after the
  cached header/signature pair verifies against the roster-derived slot leader.
  Forged cached signer indices now fall back to the real slot leader instead of
  steering exact repair toward another canonical peer.
- Hardened inbound RBC chunk repair responses. `RbcChunkRequest` handling now
  refuses to serve cached chunks from invalid, malformed, key/header-mismatched,
  or roster-leader-signature-mismatched sessions, while still answering requests
  for well-formed sessions.
- Hardened outbound missing-chunk repair so nodes no longer emit
  `RbcChunkRequest` for sessions whose cached block header/signature marker is
  absent or keyed to a different block hash, height, or view. Those sessions now
  move to missing-BlockCreated repair instead of arming the chunk-repair
  cooldown.
- Hardened production READY rebroadcast paths so broad and targeted READY repair
  only package recorded READY signatures after the cached session header/signature
  metadata matches the session key and verifies against the roster-derived
  leader. The pure `rbc_ready_bundle(...)` constructor remains available for
  already-validated low-level tests.
- Hardened inbound RBC READY and DELIVER acceptance so correctly signed peer
  evidence only mutates a live session after the cached session header/signature
  metadata matches the progress key and the leader signature verifies against
  the resolved session roster. Misbound cached sessions now drop READY/DELIVER
  evidence without recording, deferring, or completing delivery, while pre-INIT
  stashing remains unchanged.
- Hardened inbound live RBC chunk ingestion with the same metadata boundary:
  once a session exists, `RbcChunk` can only mutate it after the cached
  header/signature metadata matches the session key, the chunk shape is valid,
  and the leader signature verifies against the resolved roster. Misbound live
  sessions now drop valid-digest chunks and move to missing-`BlockCreated`
  repair instead of filling the wrong session; pre-INIT chunk stashing remains
  unchanged.
- Fixed partial-session local hydration before READY/DELIVER processing. A
  session with matching local authoritative payload but incomplete chunk slots
  now hydrates the missing chunks before root validation instead of comparing a
  partial computed chunk root with the full expected root and falsely marking
  the session invalid. Matching local payload can therefore make raw DELIVER
  evidence terminal and expose delivered-RBC validation priority immediately.
- Closed an RBC idle-scheduler liveness gap for ready-to-deliver sessions:
  complete payloads with READY quorum but no local DELIVER now wake the actor
  immediately when the local validator can build a DELIVER, while observers and
  other non-signing roles stay asleep instead of hot-looping. Complete chunk
  counters whose bytes fail the advertised payload hash, or whose leader
  signature does not verify against the session roster, stay passive as
  malformed evidence instead of arming an immediate local-DELIVER wakeup. The
  pending local-READY wakeup now uses the same roster-verified leader-signature
  boundary, so malformed leader metadata cannot force an immediate READY retry.
- Added a live partial-delivery regression for the authoritative local-payload
  fallback: raw RBC status still records the accepted DELIVER marker for
  diagnostics, but incomplete chunk counters do not satisfy authoritative
  delivered predicates or schedule validation as `rbc_deliver`.
- Added a recovery-roster regression for DA-enabled NPoS catch-up: a temporary
  deterministic recovery roster shrink now has direct coverage proving
  `on_block_commit` restores the original baseline roster at the recovery
  height and consumes the pending restore marker.
- Added block-sync batch-response adversarial matrix rows for globally enabled
  hintless sync when a specific requester lacks roster proof. Roster-hinted
  updates and plain `BlockCreated` responses now pin the forwarded
  requester-proof bit so the downstream send gate cannot authorize hintless
  `BlockSyncUpdate` traffic for unproven peers.
- Removed the stale soft fallback from the confidential combined
  downtime+timeout localnet restart-pressure test: after the restarted peer
  comes back, it must now catch up to the expected non-empty height before the
  final balance checks can pass.
- Refreshed the ZK confidential localnet shield fixtures to use deterministic
  non-empty encrypted payload envelopes. The exact restart-pressure rerun first
  exposed that the old default payloads were now rejected during shield
  execution (`ciphertext must not be empty`), leaving the public shield debit
  unapplied; the fixed fixtures exercise the production payload validator and
  restore the intended balance assertions.
- Also refreshed direct core ZK shield fixtures that were still using default
  encrypted payload envelopes, and moved the grouped confidential
  transfer/unshield event plus shield-transfer audit fixtures off the stale
  generic proof envelope. Those tests now register canonical confidential v2
  verifying keys, seed real confidential notes, build real v2 transfer/unshield
  proofs, and assert the emitted roots/commitments from production execution.
- Repaired the remaining grouped ZK scaffold/root-window fixtures reached by the
  non-empty payload sweep. `shield_burns_and_unshield_mints` now uses canonical
  confidential v2 transfer/unshield verifier records, v2 note/root material, and
  a real v2 unshield proof instead of an asset-hidden transfer proof pretending
  to authorize unshield. The root-hint window test now commits/drops each state
  block before opening the next one, and uses duplicate-nullifier validation as
  the deterministic post-root gate so stale-root rejection is tested without
  entering proof verification.
- Gated the STARK-only ZK-ACE identity-management happy path and matching
  Soracloud BFV assertion helper behind `zk-stark`. The default-feature
  `iroha_core --lib` sweep no longer executes a STARK-only verifier path or
  emits the helper dead-code warning, while the `zk-stark` focused rerun still
  covers the happy path.

## 2026-06-12 Halo2 OpenVerify reserved proof-family circuit aliases

- Hardened the generic `halo2/ipa` OpenVerify circuit-id gate so bare and
  Halo2-prefixed circuit ids that advertise reserved proof families or
  trusted-setup material reject before verifier dispatch, including `kzg`,
  `k-z-g`, `groth16`, `bn254`, `halo2/ipa:kzg`, `halo2/ipa:groth16`,
  `halo2/ipa:stark/fri`, and `halo2/pasta/kzg`.
- Extended the helper, zero-duration guardrail, and preverify/dedup matrices so
  reserved proof-family circuit aliases fail while normal bare Halo2 circuit ids
  such as `tiny-add` remain accepted.
- Trimmed the ML-DSA RNG test helper visibility in `iroha_crypto` from
  `pub(crate)` to private so strict `iroha_core` clippy can pass through the
  already-private dependency module.
- Updated `docs/source/zk_envelopes.md` to document the generic Halo2
  reserved-family circuit-id rejection alongside the existing backend and
  circuit binding rules.
- Validation:
  - `rustfmt --edition 2024 crates/iroha_core/src/zk.rs`

## 2026-06-12 ML-DSA random seed inertness regression

- Routed top-level random ML-DSA key generation through a checked
  OS-seed helper instead of the direct infallible `pqcrypto_mldsa` random
  keypair path.
- Routed top-level ML-DSA signing through the checked `soranet_pq` hedged
  signer and removed the private infallible signer shim; ML-DSA pair
  validation now compares deterministic public-key recovery output instead of
  issuing a randomized probe signature.
- Added RNG-injected regressions for ML-DSA OS entropy failure, all-zero
  generated seed rejection, and nonzero generated seed acceptance while
  preserving top-level random sign/verify and seeded all-zero coverage.
- Switched the remaining `iroha_crypto` ML-DSA public-key parse fixture away
  from a direct `pqcrypto_mldsa` random keypair and onto the checked top-level
  random route.
- Verified the separate `soranet_pq` hedged seed boundary still rejects
  all-zero required seed draws for ML-DSA keygen/signing, ML-KEM
  keygen/encapsulation, and direct hedged RNG construction.

  public rows can satisfy rendering or strict verification.

## 2026-06-12 STARK OpenVerify circuit-family guardrail binding

- Hardened STARK `OpenVerifyEnvelope` metadata gates so circuit ids must stay
  within the selected STARK backend family before generic STARK proof
  construction, full verification, zero-duration guardrail dispatch, or
  lightweight preverification. The generic `stark/fri` entry point now rejects
  circuit ids advertising another proof family, including slash and colon forms
  such as `halo2/...`, `halo2:...`, and `kzg:...`, while profile-specific STARK
  backends reject decoded circuit ids advertising a sibling STARK profile or the
  generic `stark/fri:` prefix.
- Added adversarial guardrail and preverify matrices for sibling-profile,
  generic-prefix, cross-family `halo2/ipa`, colon-form `halo2:...`, and
  colon-form trusted-setup `kzg:...` circuit spoofing. The preverify regression
  also proves failed attempts do not poison the dedup cache.
- Added `zk-stark` prover/full-verifier regressions for the same circuit-family
  mismatches so valid-looking VK payloads cannot construct or verify under
  misleading OpenVerify circuit metadata.
- Updated `docs/source/zk_envelopes.md` to document STARK circuit-family and
  profile binding beside the existing OpenVerify backend consistency rules.

  full key-entry shape and inert-entry validation remains behind the capacity
  gate.
- Direct no-artifact bounded full-bootstrap execution and bound helpers now
  preflight FullBootstrapV1 key/material metadata before rounded-capacity
  errors, without moving refresh ciphertext entry validation ahead of the
  capacity gate. Artifact-aware bounded full-bootstrap prefix execution and
  bound helpers share that key/material preflight before concrete artifact or
  ciphertext validation.
- Bounded raw-sample coefficient-zero repack and raw-sample owner diagnostic
  helpers now reject malformed raw-sample metadata before rounded-capacity
  errors, while valid raw-sample metadata still reaches the capacity gate
  before downstream secret-key checks.
- Bounded raw-sample extraction and sample-switch execution helpers now
  preflight sample/key metadata plus key/sample consistency before
  rounded-capacity errors, keeping ciphertext shapes and full switch-key entries
  behind the capacity gate.
- Validation:

## 2026-06-12 BFV execution claim inert ciphertext gate

- Hardened full-bootstrap execution proof statements and governed witness
  material so public claim input/output ciphertexts reject shape-valid all-zero
  placeholders before statement or witness material can be hashed.
- Hardened execution-prefix trace validation so externally held witness
  material also rejects all-zero intermediate trace ciphertext stages before
  public witness digests or proof-input rows can be derived.
- Hardened raw extracted sample validation so a zero constant plus all-zero
  secret-coefficient vector cannot be repacked or hashed as full-bootstrap
  witness material.
- Hardened identifier ciphertext decryption so shape-valid all-zero envelope
  slots are rejected before they can decode as zero scalars.
- Kept the base ciphertext validator shape-only so internal zero-ciphertext
  algebra remains available, while applying the non-inert gate only to
  proof-facing execution claim, trace, raw-sample material, and identifier
  envelope slots.
- Refreshed the canonical exact and bounded execution proof-statement digests
  for the current typed material and added all-zero input/output regressions at
  both statement and governed-witness layers, plus an all-zero trace-stage
  regression for public witness material hashing and an all-zero raw-sample
  regression for validation and repacking.

## 2026-06-12 BFV seeded encryption public-key inert material gate

- Hardened exact and bounded seeded BFV encryption so shape-valid public keys
  whose `b` and `a` components are both all zero fail before ciphertext
  material is generated.
- Applied the same non-inert public-key check to
  `BfvIdentifierPublicParameters::validate` and identifier encryption after
  envelope metadata, input length, and deterministic seed preflights, preserving
  existing public-input error ordering while rejecting inert identifier
  ciphertext envelopes.
- Hardened bootstrap public-key digest comparison so refresh-only bootstrap
  proof statements reject all-zero public keys even when the optional
  `public_key_digest` metadata is omitted.
- Hardened evaluation-key refresh transcript validation and digesting so exact
  and bounded transcript inventories reject all-zero public keys before the
  public key can be hashed into governance material.
- Hardened full-bootstrap material proof statement lookup so refresh-only and
  no-bootstrap `None` cases still reject all-zero public-key material before
  returning.
- Hardened exact and bounded public/secret consistency diagnostics so an
  all-zero public key can no longer satisfy residual checks by producing a zero
  residual against any secret key.

## 2026-06-11 BFV full-bootstrap native STARK/AIR wrapper binding

- Added a BFV-specific native STARK/FRI AIR prover/verifier wrapper in
  `iroha_core::zk_stark`. The prover builds from validated
  `BfvFullBootstrapExecutionProverInputMaterialV1`, derives the STARK domain
  tag from the BFV execution statement hash, pins the canonical BFV circuit id
  and FRI profile, and retries deterministic transcript labels until sampled
  openings avoid private rows.
- The verifier first runs the shared explicit AIR verifier, then decodes the
  envelope and rejects stale transcript labels, statement-domain drift,
  non-canonical BFV parameters, wrong circuit/public digest metadata, wrong
  opening counts, duplicate/private-row openings, or sampled rows that are not
  the canonical statement-bound public-padding rows.
- The wrapper regression now also forges a structurally valid generic AIR
  envelope under an allowed BFV transcript label whose sampled openings expose
  private rows; generic explicit AIR verification accepts the proof, while the
  BFV-native wrapper rejects it through the no-unmasked-private-row policy.
- STARK/FRI proof synthesis now rejects nonzero final folded layers before
  proof bytes are emitted. The public explicit-AIR prover surfaces
  `STARK final FRI value must be zero` instead of constructing an envelope that
  only fails during verifier replay.
- Generic STARK `OpenVerifyEnvelope` construction and verification now reserve
  the BFV full-bootstrap circuit id for that BFV-native path. Canonical and
  backend-prefixed BFV circuit aliases are rejected before they can fall back to
  the generic binding AIR without BFV public-padding opening checks.
- Added a feature-enabled core regression that constructs a valid BFV
  full-bootstrap prover-input package through public crypto APIs, proves it
  through the new wrapper, and checks stale domain/material/opening rejection.
  Remaining production work is still the audited BFV arithmetic
  proof-producing backend plus release-grade generated prover/verifier
  artifacts and external audit evidence.

## 2026-06-11 BFV full-bootstrap release-audit placeholder body hardening

- Tightened BFV full-bootstrap release-audit report/archive validation so
  explicit draft, `not for production`, `not production ready`, and
  `replace before production` markers, including dash/underscore variants, are
  treated as placeholder audit artifact text. The body-byte builders, signed
  package validation, package digesting, and known digest-only signoff preimage
  guard now reject those markers before release-audit evidence can be accepted
  as production material. Release-audit native proof-key payload digest sentinel
  checks reject the same draft/not-for-production/replacement markers.
- Extended governed full-bootstrap material digest sentinels to reject the same
  draft, `not for production`, `not production ready`, and
  `replace before production` marker family, including dash/underscore
  variants, before circuit material, release-audit evidence, signoffs,
  manifests, or caller-pinned package digests can be accepted.
- Hardened BFV full-bootstrap proof-key material envelope encoding and
  proof-key/envelope validation so placeholder public-input schema and evaluator
  artifact-set digest sentinels fail before native proof-key material can be
  serialized or accepted as governed proof-key metadata.
- Hardened BFV full-bootstrap blind-rotation key construction and validation so
  placeholder accumulator digest sentinels fail before packed left-rotation
  material can be encoded or admitted. Refreshed the deterministic
  artifact-bundle digest golden to the current canonical generated material.
- Hardened verifier-facing full-bootstrap material proof-profile validation so
  caller-supplied expected schema and verifier-key material commitment digests
  reject placeholder sentinels before profile comparison.
- Hardened full-bootstrap material/execution proof-input statement hash
  validation plus arithmetic public-padding row construction so placeholder
  statement-hash sentinels fail before typed proof material or AIR rows can be
  accepted. Refreshed the exact and bounded execution statement digest goldens
  to the current canonical generated material and made the alternate-artifact
  statement fixture regenerate matching proof-key artifacts.

## 2026-06-11 STARK OpenVerify verifier-key backend binding

  dispatch so the supplied `VerifyingKeyBox.backend` label must exactly match
  the requested `stark/fri/*` proof backend before verifier-key hashing,
  payload decoding, or wrapper transcript checks run. This closes a direct API
  path where a self-consistent wrapper could bind a verifier-key hash computed

## 2026-06-11 STARK OpenVerify auxiliary commitment rejection

- Tightened STARK `OpenVerifyEnvelope` verification so generated generic and
  ZK-ACE wrapper paths reject inner native STARK proofs that carry optional
  generic auxiliary composition commitments. The wrappers already reconstruct
  the AIR statement digest from outer metadata and public inputs, so accepting
  additional composition commitments would make the wrapped proof shape
  non-canonical.
- Added a regression that attaches otherwise valid auxiliary composition
  commitments to generated binding-AIR and ZK-ACE STARK wrappers and confirms
  backend verification rejects the extra material while the unmodified generated
  wrappers still verify.
- Fixed ZK-ACE STARK wrapper proof construction to pass the canonical bare
  ZK-ACE circuit id into the ZK-ACE AIR prover while retaining normalized
  circuit-id comparison for the outer wrapper and verifier key. The generated
  ZK-ACE `OpenVerifyEnvelope` now verifies under the production-floor STARK/FRI
  parameters instead of failing at constructor time with an AIR circuit-id
  mismatch.
- Bound ZK-ACE wrapper native STARK public inputs to the digest derived from
  the outer ZK-ACE public-input payload. A regenerated inner ZK-ACE STARK proof
  whose domain tag is bound to a wrong native public-input word now fails at the
  wrapper verifier instead of relying only on AIR public-digest checks.
- ZK-ACE STARK wrapper dispatch now classifies circuit ids after STARK backend
  normalization and rejects non-canonical ZK-ACE circuit aliases. Generic STARK
  `OpenVerifyEnvelope` construction also refuses to target the ZK-ACE circuit,
  so a prefixed alias cannot fall back to the generic binding AIR verifier.
- STARK `OpenVerifyEnvelope` verification now pins the inner AIR transcript label
  to the canonical wrapper domain (`IROHA-STARK-AIR-V1` for generic binding AIR,
  `IROHA-STARK-ZK-ACE-AIR-V1` for ZK-ACE). Regenerated proofs under alternate
  transcript labels are rejected even when their FRI transcript is otherwise
  internally valid.
- The STARK `ivm-execution-v1` proof helper now gates the requested circuit id
  after STARK backend normalization before it builds an IVM execution wrapper, so
  a caller cannot provide a matching non-IVM STARK verifier key and emit an
  IVM-shaped proof under another circuit id.
- Generic STARK `OpenVerifyEnvelope` construction and verification now also
  reject below-floor STARK/FRI verifier-key payloads before accepting generated
  wrapper proofs.

## 2026-06-11 STARK auxiliary composition digest binding

- Tightened native STARK/FRI generic composition verification so accepted
  auxiliary composition entries must rederive the AIR public digest from their
  constant, final-fold coefficient, and auxiliary terms. A wire-index retarget
  that preserves Merkle leaf arithmetic now fails unless it is also bound to the
  statement digest.
- Added focused generic composition regressions for auxiliary wire ordering. The
  proof constructor now has explicit coverage that duplicate or unsorted
  auxiliary wire indices fail before envelope construction, and the verifier has
  a tamper regression showing duplicate auxiliary wire indices are rejected even
  when the arithmetic composition leaf value is otherwise unchanged.
- Validation:
  - `cargo test -j 1 -p iroha_core --features zk-stark,zk-tests stark_rejects_auxiliary_composition_wire_retarget_without_digest_match --test iroha_core_group_05 -- --nocapture`

    (`1` passed, `31` filtered out)

    (`1` passed, `31` filtered out)

## 2026-06-11 SCCP copied filename whitespace hardening

- Reconfirmed SCCP launch scope remains limited to Ethereum, BSC, Solana, TON,
  and TRON; SCCP will not support Sub&#115;trate/Pol&#107;adot networks for now.
- Tightened SCCP release-bundle source preflights so copied evidence inputs,
  corridor phase logs, and native prover bundle manifests reject basenames with
  surrounding whitespace before any file is copied into public bundle paths.
  The copied-name helper now enforces the same rule defensively during artifact
  naming.
- Added CLI regressions for padded evidence input filenames, padded corridor
  phase-evidence filenames, padded native prover manifest filenames, and padded
  native prover payload filenames, and pinned the source filename whitespace
  markers in the source-copy and release artifact path-text source inventories.
- Redacted duplicate top-level evidence input path diagnostics to
  `<path> duplicates <path>` before source copying, with a secret-token
  regression so canonical-path alias rejection does not leak local operator
  directory names.
- Added category-only percent-encoded traversal rejection before copying
  evidence inputs, corridor phase logs, or native prover bundle manifests, and
  before native prover payload source resolution from manifest-relative paths,
  with secret-token regressions for each source class.
- Redacted symlinked source-path and source-ancestor diagnostics for evidence
  inputs, corridor phase logs, native prover manifests, and native prover
  payload sources before source copying. The focused regressions now place
  `secret-token` in each symlink path family and assert stderr keeps it out.
- Redacted symlinked output-directory and output-ancestor diagnostics before
  bundle creation or forced replacement. The output-path regressions now place
  `secret-token` in symlinked output targets and assert stderr keeps it out.
- Redacted local source/output control-character diagnostics while preserving
  the offending control-byte label. Evidence input, corridor phase-log, native
  prover manifest, and output-directory regressions now place `secret-token` in
  the rejected local path and assert stderr keeps it out.
- Redacted Markdown-unsafe copied source filename diagnostics before source
  copying. Evidence input and corridor phase-log regressions now place
  `secret-token` in pipe-containing filenames and assert stderr keeps it out,
  while the copied-name helper also avoids echoing rejected names.
- Redacted forced output replacement containment diagnostics. The regression now
  places `secret-token` in the output root containing protected evidence and
  asserts stderr keeps both output and input path text out.
- Redacted existing-output diagnostics when `--force` is omitted. The regression
  now builds a complete preflight bundle against an existing
  `secret-token` output directory and asserts stderr keeps the target path out.
- Redacted dangerous-root and repository-containing output diagnostics. The
  regressions now target the repository root and its parent and assert stderr
  keeps local repository paths out.
- Redacted native EVM prover role-reuse diagnostics across bundle generation,
  readiness JSON blockers, and published-bundle verification. The regressions
  now reuse `secret-token` native prover artifact paths and assert diagnostics
  keep the path text out while still naming the conflicting roles.
- Redacted copied artifact-integrity, manifest/report artifact membership, and
  release-notes attachment artifact-list diagnostics so adversarial bundle
  artifact paths do not leak through public verifier output.
- Redacted manifest artifact-row validation, extracted bundle-entry validation,
  duplicate/unmanifested bundle entry diagnostics, and manifested artifact
  symlink checks. The focused verifier regressions now place `secret-token` in
  duplicate, unmanifested, malformed, and symlinked bundle artifact paths and
  assert strict verifier output keeps that path text out.
- Redacted generated release artifact path diagnostics in the bundle,
  readiness, and strict-verifier helpers. Direct bundle and readiness
  regressions now reject symlinked, control-character, Markdown-unsafe,
  padded, and percent-encoded artifact paths containing `secret-token` without
  echoing that path text.
- Redacted copied input provenance and readiness-report input/input-artifact
  path diagnostics, including copied-input recomputation exception text. The
  adversarial regressions now place `secret-token` in duplicate, escaping,
  layout-drifted, control-character, Markdown-unsafe, padded, and
  percent-encoded report paths and assert bundle/verifier output omits it.
- Redacted native EVM prover manifest-relative payload path diagnostics for
  control-character and Markdown-unsafe path text in the bundle builder,
  readiness generator, and strict verifier. The new regressions put
  `secret-token` into malformed `proof_artifact` paths and assert generated
  blockers and verifier output omit it.
- Redacted missing, non-regular, unreadable, and forbidden-marker scan native
  prover payload diagnostics so valid-looking manifest-relative paths and local
  exception text are not echoed. The focused tests now put `secret-token` into
  missing `proof_artifact`, parity fixture, and self-test payload paths across
  bundle generation, readiness JSON, and strict verification.

  query helper height selection.

## 2026-06-11 SCCP phase assignment no-trim hardening

- Tightened SCCP release readiness and release-bundle phase assignment parsing
  so `--phase-result` and `--phase-evidence` phase names, plus
  `--phase-result` status values, reject padded or whitespace spellings instead
  of trim-normalizing them into canonical corridor phases or statuses. Phase
  names now also reject Markdown-unsafe or malformed values before diagnostics
  can echo operator input. Unknown phase names and unknown phase-result
  statuses use category-only diagnostics instead of echoing Markdown-unsafe
  operator input. The
  release-bundle generator fails before output copy/render when phase-evidence
  names are malformed, direct readiness and bundle CLI tests now cover both
  Markdown-unsafe and malformed phase names, and malformed phase-assignment
  syntax now uses fixed diagnostics without echoing table-breaking operator
  strings. Duplicate phase-evidence diagnostics now redact local evidence paths
  as `<path>` so operator-local filenames cannot leak while reporting source
  conflicts, and missing `--phase-evidence-dir` logs report standard checked
  layouts without echoing the operator-supplied directory. The source-inventory
  guard pins the no-trim and no-echo diagnostics alongside duplicate
  phase-evidence detection.
- Validation:
  - `python3 -m py_compile scripts/sccp_release_readiness_report.py scripts/sccp_release_bundle.py scripts/sccp_verify_release_bundle.py pytests/scripts/sccp_release_readiness_report_test.py pytests/scripts/sccp_release_bundle_test.py`

## 2026-06-11 STARK AIR metadata admission hardening

- Tightened native STARK/FRI metadata admission so transcript labels, domain
  tags, and AIR circuit ids now have to be non-empty, bounded, printable ASCII
  strings without whitespace. Proof construction, query-shape replay, and
  decoded-envelope verification reject noncanonical transcript metadata before
  transcript sampling or verification.
- Bound the ZK-ACE AIR prover/verifier path to the canonical ZK-ACE circuit id,
  so a well-formed AIR envelope cannot be retargeted to a wrong circuit string
  while preserving rows, roots, and public digest.
- Production STARK/FRI verifier-key payload admission now rejects malformed
  expected and embedded circuit ids before equality, so matching noncanonical
  identifiers cannot satisfy the verifier-key floor.
- Caller-provided STARK verifier limits now only tighten canonical structure
  caps: oversized domain/blowup depths, query counts, Merkle depths, AIR row
  widths, auxiliary composition terms, domain tags, transcript labels, and
  encoded envelope byte sizes stay rejected even if a custom limit tries to
  raise the ceiling.

  public record constructor with report/archive digests aliasing signed release
  commitments, and repeats report/archive aliasing across every signed

## 2026-06-12 Kagemusha release manifest timestamp hardening

- Hardened `kagemusha_release_bundle.py --verify-existing` so the top-level
  readiness summary, release manifest, and lineage/compact evidence-section
  `generated_at_utc` values must remain canonical UTC, and so readiness-summary
  maximum generated/signed timestamp bounds cannot be future-dated beyond the
  release validator clock-skew allowance. Ordinary top-level release-manifest
  timestamp refresh is still ignored by the stable manifest comparison.
- Added adversarial coverage for a future-dated existing release manifest
  timestamp, future-dated nested release-manifest evidence-section timestamp,
  and malformed/future-dated nested readiness-summary evidence-section
  timestamps, including moving `max_generated_at_utc` and Android
  `max_signed_at_utc` fields, and pinned the new blockers in the
  production-readiness guard.
- Hardened Android readiness-summary slot lists so release bundles require
  accepted, safe, unique, sorted slot report entries whose inventory matches the
  signed-evidence map before Android artifacts are packaged.
- Hardened Android slot Kagemusha detail validation so release-critical
  timestamps, digests, artifact paths, native ABI, device family, and fields
  mirrored into the signed-evidence summary are checked before packaging, and
  the slot family inventory must exactly match `covered_device_families`.

## 2026-06-12 Identifier receipt timestamp exactness and Swift decode follow-up

- Fixed Swift identifier receipt JSON decoding so `payload.account_id` is no
  longer trimmed before signed receipt verification; padded account ids now fail
  during decode.
- Hardened Python and JavaScript canonical receipt timestamp handling so padded
  numeric strings for `payload.execution.executed_at_ms`,
  `payload.execution.expires_at_ms`,
  `payload.opening.payload.opened_at_ms`, and
  `payload.opening.payload.expires_at_ms` are rejected before canonical receipt
  bytes are encoded or verified.
- Hardened Kotlin/JVM and Android Java receipt timestamp handling so negative
  `Long` values cannot be parsed from Torii JSON or passed through direct
  canonical builders into fields encoded as receipt u64 values, and so oversized
  Android Java numeric strings cannot wrap through `BigInteger.longValue()`.
- Added timestamp exactness mutations to the Python shared-vector receipt test
  and JavaScript identifier receipt suite, added the JS receipt-local exact
  unsigned-integer helper, and pinned the behavior with
  `--negative-control-identifier-receipt-timestamp-exactness-guard`.
- Added negative timestamp-u64 mutations to the Kotlin/JVM and Android Java
  canonical/parser tests, and pinned the behavior with
  `--negative-control-identifier-receipt-timestamp-u64-guard`.
- Wired the timestamp negative control into the payload-bench workflow and
  JavaScript meta-test inventory, and added the C# Windows mirror TODO to
  `roadmap.md`.

## 2026-06-11 Compact key generator-log path preflight

- Hardened `scripts/kagemusha_recursive_compact_key_evidence.py` so direct
  compact-key evidence helper calls reject secret-looking, control-character,
  missing, symlinked, hardlinked, non-regular, or unreadable
  `generator_log_path` values before hashing compact artifacts or reading the
  generator log, and the generator-log validator rejects unsafe
  `--artifact-dir` strings before resolving while resolving only the log parent
  before local file-shape validation. Direct compact-key builder calls now
  reject explicitly unsafe `generator_log_path` strings before artifact-dir
  metadata reads.
- Hardened lineage and compact-key evidence helper output-corridor validators
  so direct `--out` or `--artifact-dir` control-character paths fail before
  any `Path.resolve()` corridor check.
- Hardened lineage proof-log input validation so unsafe `--proof-log` strings
  fail before artifact-directory metadata reads or traversal.
- Hardened release-bundle relative-path calculation so direct callers reject
  secret-looking or control-character evidence and bundle-root strings before
  any `Path.resolve()` release-inventory check, and release evidence entries now
  run bundle-root containment before digesting evidence bytes.
- Hardened the standalone Android device-lab scanner CLI so unsafe explicit
  `--slot` values fail before root classification, and unsafe
  `--trusted-signer-public-key` strings fail with the other path arguments
  before slot discovery or signer loading.
- Hardened direct Android production metadata validation so unsafe
  trusted-signer public-key path strings in caller-provided signer maps fail
  before slot metadata reads.
- Hardened the readiness Android rollup so direct trusted-signer maps are
  validated before Android root classification and only canonical signer-key
  SHA-256 ids are reflected in summaries.
- Hardened direct release-bundle builders so unsafe trusted-signer maps fail
  before bundle-root metadata reads; hardened release-bundle verification so
  the same unsafe maps fail before manifest loading. Blocked manifests only
  reflect canonical signer-key SHA-256 ids.
- Hardened release-bundle verification so lineage and compact section
  digest/size maps must exactly match the canonical artifact and proof-log
  inventories instead of accepting well-formed extra or missing keys until the
  later drift comparison.
- Hardened release-bundle verification so `lineage_key_release_tooling`
  `checked_files` must exactly match the required release-tooling inventory
  instead of accepting well-formed extra or missing marker files until the later
  drift comparison.
- Hardened release-bundle verification so ABI-6 manifest path/schema/bridge
  version/operation count and the ABI-7 recursive compact circuit id fail with
  field-specific section-value blockers before the generic manifest-drift
  comparison.
- Hardened release-bundle verification so ABI-6 projected limits and modes must
  match the required release values exactly, instead of accepting arbitrary
  object-shaped maps until the later drift comparison.
- Hardened direct release-bundle build and verify calls so unsafe `repo_root`
  values fail before bundle-root metadata reads or readiness/release manifest
  loading.
- Hardened release-bundle verification so Android signed-evidence release
  entries must match the signed-evidence summary path/digest and freshly
  computed release-evidence size before generic manifest-drift comparison.
- Hardened release-bundle verification so Android slot artifact release entries
  must also match the signed-evidence summary path/digest and freshly computed
  release-evidence size before generic manifest-drift comparison.
- Hardened release-bundle readiness-summary comparison and verification so
  Android summary fields, including `duplicate_bindings`, the per-slot `signed_evidence` map,
  device-family lists, and trusted signer digest fields, must match freshly computed device-lab evidence before generic summary or
  manifest-drift comparison.
- Hardened release-bundle readiness-summary comparison so Android covered
  device-family summary fields must match freshly computed device-lab evidence
  before generic summary drift.
- Hardened release-bundle readiness-summary shape validation so Android matrix
  lists and trusted-signer digest lists must be non-empty-string lists with the
  exact standard matrix and unique sorted non-zero lowercase SHA-256 signer
  digests before drift comparison.
- Hardened release-bundle readiness-summary shape validation so the top-level
  `generated_at` timestamp must use canonical UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` form
  and stay within the allowed future-skew window before release evidence is
  packaged.
- Hardened release-bundle readiness-summary comparison so Android
  signed-evidence slot inventory and per-slot fields must match freshly
  computed device-lab evidence with Android-specific blockers before generic
  summary drift.
- Hardened release-bundle readiness-summary comparison so lineage and compact
  evidence digest/size maps must match local release evidence with
  section-evidence drift blockers before generic summary drift.
- Hardened release-bundle readiness-summary comparison so ABI-6, ABI-7,
  lineage release-tooling, lineage metadata including the required test
  inventory, and compact metadata including record namespace/version fields
  must match local release evidence with section-value drift blockers before
  generic summary drift.
- Hardened existing release-bundle manifest verification so ABI-6, ABI-7,
  lineage tooling, lineage proof evidence, and compact-key evidence section
  values must match freshly computed release evidence with section value
  binding blockers before generic manifest drift.
- Hardened release-bundle verification so lineage and compact release artifact
  entries, proof-log entries, and the compact generator-log entry must match
  expected bundle-relative paths plus their release-section digest and size
  fields before generic manifest-drift comparison.
- Hardened release-bundle verification so compact generator-log artifact digest
  and size maps must match freshly computed compact evidence before generic
  manifest-drift comparison.
- Hardened release-bundle verification so top-level readiness-summary, lineage
  evidence, compact evidence JSON, and compact generator-log entries must use
  the canonical release-packet filenames, digest, and size fields from freshly
  computed release evidence before generic manifest-drift comparison.
- Hardened release-bundle build validation so Android signed-evidence summary
  fields must match freshly validated device-lab evidence before generic
  summary drift, giving safe but forged slot artifact paths a field-specific
  signed-evidence drift blocker.
- Hardened Android device-lab explicit slot selection so duplicate `--slot`
  ids are rejected before root discovery or slot scanning can double-count a
  physical evidence directory in matrix summaries.
- Hardened direct Android slot discovery so callers that bypass the CLI still
  validate and deduplicate explicit slot ids before joining them to the
  device-lab root.
- Hardened the production readiness rollup's explicit Android slot selection
  path with the same duplicate-slot preflight before Android root
  classification.
- Hardened Android device-lab root discovery so slots are sorted by directory
  name before scanning, keeping JSON summaries and release-bundle inputs stable
  across filesystem iteration order.
- Hardened Android device-lab top-level slot artifact enumeration so symlink,
  hardlink, and special-file diagnostics are also produced in stable path order.
- Hardened Android device-lab and readiness-rollup summary construction so
  release-facing JSON copies direct report dictionaries through a
  secret/control-string/non-finite-number sanitizer, duplicate binding slots
  render through safe slot labels, redacted report-key collisions preserve the
  first value and emit explicit diagnostics, malformed direct report statuses
  normalize to failed rows instead of tracebacks, non-string direct report keys
  normalize to explicit placeholders before JSON rendering, non-finite direct
  report numbers are redacted before strict JSON serialization, unsupported
  direct report values are normalized to explicit placeholders, malformed
  direct report error lists normalize to explicit safe placeholders before
  slot-invalid blockers reflect them, malformed direct Kagemusha report sections normalize to empty non-evidence objects,
  unsafe direct binding slot labels are redacted in duplicate and malformed-digest blockers,
  malformed direct binding digests are rejected before duplicate checks,
  device-family values must be canonical strings before they count toward
  matrix coverage, and duplicate binding digest values plus trusted-signer
  summary keys must be canonical lowercase SHA-256 hex before they can be reflected. Direct
  signed-evidence summary fields are also revalidated before reflection: timestamps must be canonical
  UTC, digest fields must be non-zero lowercase SHA-256, and artifact paths
  must be canonical safe relative paths. Multiple validated reports that
  collapse to the same redacted signed-evidence summary slot label now fail
  closed instead of overwriting each other in the summary object.
- Added adversarial regressions proving unsafe custom, missing, and symlinked
  generator-log paths do not invoke artifact or generator-log readers and do
  not leak unsafe path bytes in diagnostics, plus a shared output-corridor
  regression and release-bundle relative-path regression proving unsafe paths
  fail before resolution.
- Added direct and CLI duplicate-slot regressions proving repeated explicit
  slot ids fail closed without scanning the slot or emitting a traceback.
- Added a direct `discover_slots` regression proving duplicate and traversal
  slot ids fail before root listing or root-relative path construction.
- Added a readiness-rollup duplicate-slot regression proving repeated Android
  slot ids fail before root classification.
- Added a deterministic-discovery regression that forces reverse filesystem
  iteration and proves scanner reports are emitted in sorted slot order.
  Added the same reverse-iteration coverage for top-level slot artifact
  enumeration.
- Added direct summary regressions proving unsafe direct report slot strings and
  nested summary strings are redacted, control-character report strings are
  redacted, non-finite report numbers are redacted, malformed direct binding
  digests are blocked before duplicate checks, unsafe direct binding slot labels
  are redacted in duplicate and malformed-digest blockers, and non-SHA
  duplicate-binding values are ignored before summary JSON rendering. The same
  direct summary coverage proves non-SHA trusted-signer keys are dropped before
  rendering, and direct signed-evidence summary fields with malformed
  timestamps, unsafe paths, zero/uppercase digests, missing fields, unsafe
  slots, secret-looking values, or colliding redacted slot labels are rejected
  or omitted before rendering. Scanner and readiness direct-report regressions
  now also prove redacted report-key collisions preserve the first value,
  block or mark the summary, and do not leak the unsafe keys.
  Scanner summary coverage now also proves missing or noncanonical direct
  report statuses normalize to failed rows instead of raising exceptions.
  Scanner and readiness regressions now prove non-string direct report keys
  normalize to explicit placeholders, preserve the first value on collisions,
  and remain strict-JSON serializable.
  Scanner direct-summary coverage now also proves non-finite report numbers are
  redacted before `allow_nan=False` JSON rendering.
  Scanner and readiness direct-summary coverage now also proves unsupported
  Python values such as bytes, paths, objects, and sets normalize to explicit
  placeholders before strict JSON rendering.
  Scanner and readiness direct-report coverage now also proves malformed
  `errors` fields normalize to safe string-list placeholders before JSON
  rendering or slot-invalid blocker reflection.
  Scanner and readiness direct-report coverage now also proves malformed
  Kagemusha sections cannot satisfy matrix coverage or crash duplicate-binding
  scans.
  Scanner and readiness coverage now also proves list-valued, secret-looking,
  or unknown direct device-family values do not satisfy the standard Android
  matrix.
- Updated the Kagemusha guard, offline guide, and roadmap for the direct

## 2026-06-11 Kagemusha Android harness canonicalization

- Hardened the signed-slot assembler and production slot scanner so preserved
  `attestation/harness-result.json` strings are accepted only in their exact
  canonical form. Slot aliases cannot carry surrounding whitespace,
  StrongBox/KeyMint level labels must already match the accepted labels, and
  harness `challenge_hex` must be lowercase hexadecimal without whitespace.
  This keeps raw pulls, signed-slot assembly, the attestation report renderer,
  and production scanning aligned on one fail-closed harness policy.
- Replaced the scanner's slot-tree traversal with a direct `os.scandir` walker
  that records each no-follow directory entry and reports traversal failures as
  `slot directory could not be listed`, without depending on `Path.rglob()` or
  `Path.is_dir()` behavior.
- Tightened explicit scanner `--slot` selection so supplied slot IDs must
  already be exact safe directory names without whitespace or non-printing
  control characters; unsafe values are rejected before path join instead of
  being trimmed or echoed.
- Tightened discovered scanner slot-name handling so whitespace-bearing and
  control-character-bearing slot directory names are rejected before metadata
  traversal, matching explicit `--slot` canonicalization and redacting unsafe
  labels in diagnostics and summaries.
- Tightened raw-puller and production telemetry validation so
  `telemetry/telemetry.json` `slot_id` must exactly match the slot directory
  name; whitespace-normalized telemetry bindings are rejected before raw-slot
  assembly or production scanning.
- Tightened production `slot.json` required string validation so path, digest,
  and identity fields are rejected if they require surrounding-whitespace
  trimming or contain non-printing control characters.
- Tightened signed-evidence string validation so slot-bound values and
  signature metadata are rejected if they require whitespace trimming or carry
  non-printing control characters before comparison or verification.
- Tightened production `attestation/result.json` string validation so slot
  bindings, status values, identity digests, and StrongBox labels are exact and
  cannot rely on trimming or case normalization.
- Tightened production `attestation/report.json` string validation so verifier
  status, verifier labels, and slot-bound identity fields follow the same exact
  no-trim/no-case-normalization policy.
- Tightened preserved `attestation/harness-result.json` string validation so
  non-printing control characters are rejected before raw-slot assembly or
  production scanning trusts aliases, StrongBox labels, or challenge text.
- Wired source markers, the PR workflow, and production-readiness negative
  controls for the scanner and slot-assembler harness canonicalization gates.

## 2026-06-11 Kagemusha evidence validator temp-file fallback

- Hardened the Reserved-lineage proof and ABI-7 recursive compact evidence
  document validators so temporary validation-file write failures are still
  cleaned up when a wrapped temp-file object does not expose `fileno()`. The
  normal production path continues to identity-bind cleanup through `fstat()`;
  wrapped temp files fall back to regular-file `lstat()` identity before
  returning the structured write-failure blocker.
- Fixed an order-dependent scripts-test leak where direct monkeypatches on the
  concrete `Path` class could shadow inherited `Path` methods after a test
  restored them by assignment. The Android device-lab and Kagemusha readiness
  test classes now clear those concrete method shadows before and after each
  test, so later metadata-failure tests patch the intended filesystem branch.
- Current artifact-generation state: the ABI-7 recursive compact key artifact
  job and the Reserved-lineage init key-artifact job are still active and were
  not interrupted. A read-only check found them still CPU-bound after roughly
  13h50m and 14h27m respectively; the checked recursive-compact artifact
  directory remains empty, and the lineage staged artifact directory still only
  contains temporary log files, so neither job has published release files yet.
- Audited the non-C# Kagemusha accumulator/SDK guard surface while the artifact
  jobs run. The data-model accumulator tests already cover append-boundary
  digest blanking, boundary-free public-input hashes, digest-only append
  rejection, self-consistent forged boundaries, and semantic-vs-lineage
  public-input mismatches, so this pass focused on proving the SDK guard rails
  that keep accumulator digests native-owned across Swift, Kotlin/JVM, Android

## 2026-06-11 Kagemusha attestation report input canonicalization

- Hardened the Android attestation verifier report renderer so
  `attestation/harness-result.json` `challenge_hex` and
  `--expected-challenge-hex` must already be lowercase hexadecimal without
  whitespace; StrongBox/KeyMint level labels must be exact accepted labels;
  PEM certificate-chain length must match the attestation harness `chain_length`;
  slot id, device fingerprint, OS build, app package, and verifier arguments
  must be exact whitespace-free strings; and
  `--attestation-certificate-chain-path` must be an exact whitespace-free
  slot-relative path. The renderer now rejects whitespace-normalized or
  uppercase challenge input, normalized StrongBox/KeyMint level labels,
  PEM chain-length mismatches, whitespace-normalized identity input, and
  whitespace-normalized chain-path input before hashing it or writing
  `attestation/report.json`,
  matching the raw-puller and signed-slot scanner canonical challenge policy.
- Wired source markers, the PR workflow, and production-readiness negative
  controls for the standalone renderer's canonical challenge, StrongBox level,
  chain-length, identity, and chain-path gates.

## 2026-06-11 Kagemusha production-width keygen memory reduction

- Added lower-memory key-generation-only verifier-slice shape circuits for
  Kagemusha Reserved-lineage one-hop init and append Halo2 IPA key derivation.
  The production proving and verification circuits remain unchanged; the shape
  wrappers reuse the same configuration and fixed-column/selector layout while
  streaming small default sub-witnesses during VK/PK generation.
- Switched the recursive spend lineage init/append verifier-key, proving-key,
  and cached proving-key derivation paths to the keygen-shape wrappers so
  production-width LEN=128 key-artifact generation no longer materializes the
  full recursive verifier witness tree during keygen.
- Added expensive ignored equivalence tests that compare processed verifier-key
  bytes from the full one-hop/append circuits against the keygen-shape circuits.
  These are ignored by default because the focused check takes about an hour on
  this host, but they were run explicitly before being marked ignored.
- Rebuilt the release `iroha` CLI with the new shape path and restarted the
  staged Reserved-lineage LEN=128 init key-artifact run. As of the latest
  read-only process check, the replacement init keygen is still CPU-bound and
  has not produced final staged artifacts yet. The external ABI-7 recursive
  compact keygen retry is also still running, so Android physical-device
  evidence collection is deferred to avoid adding load while both crypto jobs
  are active.
- Hardened the staged Reserved-lineage and ABI-7 recursive compact runners so
  long-running child commands write stdout/stderr directly to the identity-bound
  temporary log file instead of through a supervisor-owned pipe. This preserves
  the fail-closed staged-output contract while reducing the chance that an
  interrupted supervisor leaves a crypto child with a broken output pipe. The
  production-readiness guard now also forbids the old staged-runner
  `subprocess.PIPE`, `process.stdout.read`, and `sys.stdout.buffer` patterns so
  Python-side output mirroring cannot silently return.
- Revalidated the existing Pixel 6 / Android 16 signed physical-device slot
  with the pinned lab public key. The attached Pixel 6 also exported the
  current raw device-lab slot into
  `target/kagemusha-android-raw/google-pixel-6-6a-physical-1781077370103`;
  the raw handoff, wallet-integrity, telemetry, queue, runtime log, StrongBox
  harness, and certificate-chain artifacts byte-match the signed slot, and the
  attestation result fields match after JSON formatting is ignored. The full
  standard Android matrix is still incomplete: Pixel 7, Pixel 8, Pixel
  Fold/Tablet, Samsung Galaxy S23, and Samsung Galaxy S24 production-evidence
  slots are missing.
- The Android signed-slot assembler now publishes completed staged slots
  through directory file descriptors pinned to the captured device-lab root,
  temp-parent, and staged-slot identities and fsyncs the root descriptor, so
  path swaps before final publish fail closed. It also syncs copied-artifact
  parents and reads staged copies back through opened-file identity bindings
  before manifesting. Its normalized attestation and slot metadata JSON writes
  now use fsynced temporary files, identity-bound parent fsync, and opened-file
  readback before manifesting. Temporary staging cleanup now revalidates the
  captured temp-parent identity before removing anything and reports removal
  failures as structured blockers.
- Tightened the Android raw-pull evidence chain so the tarred
  `latest-slot.txt` and the initial `run-as cat` latest-slot query must both be
  exactly the selected slot id plus a trailing newline; whitespace-normalized
  matches are rejected before raw artifacts can be assembled into signed
  production evidence. Tar directory entries that collide with extracted files
  now return structured raw-puller errors instead of tracebacks, top-level raw
  artifacts move through opened stage/final directory descriptors, temporary
  extraction cleanup revalidates the captured temp-directory identity before
  removal, and unreviewed
  extra files or directories under the raw slot are rejected, and raw
  `attestation/result.json` must carry both `slot` and `slot_id` matching the
  selected slot id plus canonical lowercase SHA-256 chain/challenge digests
  matching the pulled StrongBox certificate chain and challenge bytes. Raw
  `attestation/result.json` is closed-schema, and the raw
  `attestation/challenge.hex` file itself must be lowercase hexadecimal with
  exactly one trailing newline; unexpected result fields, uppercase challenges,
  whitespace-normalized challenge files, noncanonical raw identity strings,
  malformed app-signing/policy digests, and downgraded raw StrongBox security
  levels are rejected before evidence assembly. The puller also validates the
  required queue, telemetry, D2D handoff, and wallet integrity JSON artifacts as
  slot-bound strict JSON before assembly; D2D must remain offline-offline with
  double-spend rejection, and wallet integrity must prove one-use key rotation
  plus rollback rejection. Raw `telemetry/status.ndjson` is parsed with
  duplicate-key and non-finite rejection, status strings must be exact lowercase
  values without surrounding whitespace or control characters, failure statuses
  are rejected, and status slot bindings must be exact strings matching the slot
  when present. `logs/runtime.log` must contain the completion marker while
  excluding build/test/panic/traceback/fatal failure markers. The raw-pull
  summary writer now rejects non-finite JSON and
  oversized payloads before temporary-file creation, then fsyncs the summary
  bytes, atomically replaces the destination, verifies readback through an
  opened-file identity binding that rejects symlinks, hardlinks, and path swaps,
  and fsyncs the identity-bound parent directory. Summary `artifact_sha256`
  inventory must include every required raw artifact, and each digest is
  collected through a separate opened-file identity binding that rejects
  symlinks, hardlinks, and file swaps after raw slot validation. The raw slot
  installer now rechecks the destination after validation, creates the final
  slot directory exclusively with owner-only permissions, moves only expected top-level artifact
  directories, binds the created slot-directory identity through each parent-fd
  slot-entry stat, move, and slot fsync, binds the output-root identity through
  the parent fsync, and deletes partial installs through the identity-bound
  output-root file descriptor only when the destination entry still names the
  directory created by the puller, reporting cleanup failures with the install
  error. The raw `latest-slot.txt` writer also fsyncs
  file bytes, atomically replaces the output, verifies readback through an
  opened-file identity binding that rejects symlinks, hardlinks, and path
  swaps, and fsyncs the identity-bound output root. The raw puller's host
  `latest-slot.txt` and summary writers now also report identity-bound temp
  cleanup failures and refuse to unlink a temp output whose file identity
  changed before cleanup. The raw puller also reports temporary extraction
  directory cleanup failures before publishing host `latest-slot.txt` or a
  pull summary. The readiness summary and
  release-bundle writers now also bind failed temporary cleanup and the output
  parent directory identity before the post-replace fsync, rejecting temp/output
  parent swaps before readback can publish a summary or manifest. The
  Reserved-lineage proof evidence helper now applies the same identity-bound
  temporary cleanup and parent sync before publishing
  `lineage-proof-evidence.json`, and the ABI-7 compact-key evidence helper does
  the same before publishing `recursive-compact-key-evidence.json`. The Android
  device-lab scanner JSON summary writer also identity-binds failed temporary
  cleanup and output-parent sync before accepting a local `--json-out` summary.
  The Android attestation report writer and signed-evidence helper now
  identity-bind failed temporary cleanup and use the same captured-parent
  identity check before accepting `attestation/report.json`,
  `evidence/signed-evidence.json`, or rewritten `sha256sum.txt` outputs. The
  signed-slot assembler now applies the same identity-bound temp cleanup to
  local slot metadata JSON outputs. The
  lineage and compact-key staged runners also identity-bind parent fsyncs for
  their child-log installs, exit markers, elapsed files, and JSON metadata
  before readback, and now identity-bind resume/replace cleanup plus temporary
  log/output cleanup before unlinking stale staged paths. The lineage and
  compact-key evidence helpers now also identity-bind validation scratch-file
  cleanup under `--artifact-dir`. Both staged finalizers
  identity-bind the published
  artifact directory before their final fsync and revalidate temporary staging
  directory identity before cleanup. Finalizer rollback cleanup now also
  removes only published files whose current identity still matches the
  publish-time identity captured immediately after install, and rollback
  cleanup failures are returned with the original publish failure. Finalizer
  temporary staging cleanup now reports removal failures and can block success
  while still preserving temp directories whose identity changed before
  cleanup.

## 2026-06-11 Jindo production privacy helper hardening

- Added Python and JavaScript adversarial coverage for the production Jindo
  lattice PCS helper boundary: production envelopes are rejected by the
  dev-fixture verifier, dev-fixture envelopes are rejected by the production
  verifier, dev fixture proof bytes cannot be repackaged under the production
  backend, and explicit non-Jindo backend overrides fail closed.
- Confirmed the Python privacy catalog now treats Jindo's exported production
  builder/verifier entrypoints as the capability source instead of vacuously
  passing on an empty planned-entrypoint list.
- Kept VeRange production helpers internal while `buildVeRangeProofV1` remains
  a planned entrypoint, preserving the invariant that planned production
  privacy entrypoints are not package-root exports until gates pass.
- Added focused Python coverage for the private VeRange production prototype
  boundary and aligned the privacy SDK guard so VeRange remains a component
  with dev-fixture/local-verifier exports plus a planned production builder.

## 2026-06-11 Sumeragi first-delivery threshold classifier

- Added
  `RbcDeliveryEntryCommitEvidenceBranchAlwaysMatchesThresholdClassifier` to the
  Sumeragi formal model and wired it into the fast, deep, and TLC-fast configs.
  The theorem proves that the first-delivery commit-evidence branch selector is
  exactly the live vote/stake threshold classifier: certified delivery is
  equivalent to both live vote and stake quorum being present after delivery,
  while pending delivery is equivalent to a missing live vote or stake threshold
  and keeps certificate witnesses empty.

## 2026-06-10 WSL cargo-test memory hardening

- Root-caused the WSL crash during `cargo test` to compile-time RSS spikes, not
  test execution: `iroha_data_model` reached about `10 GiB` RSS and
  `iroha_core --lib --test` reached about `9.5 GiB` RSS in a serialized
  `cargo test -p iroha_core --lib --no-run -j1` repro.
- Made the workspace-inherited `iroha_data_model` dependency carry only the JSON
  feature. Crates must now request heavier data-model features explicitly, and
  `iroha_p2p` no longer re-enables the data-model default feature set.
- Kept the 197k-line private Sumeragi main-loop unit-test harness available but
  moved it behind `iroha_core`'s explicit `sumeragi-main-loop-tests` feature, so
  plain local `cargo test` no longer compiles that oversized harness by default.
- Validation: `/usr/bin/time -v cargo test -p iroha_core --lib --no-run -j1
  --message-format=short` completed in 7m58s after the final hardening patch.
  Maximum RSS was `11,206,596 KiB` (~10.7 GiB), still dominated by
  `iroha_data_model`; `iroha_core --lib --test` was observed around `7.9 GiB`
  after the private Sumeragi harness was gated out.

  nonzero `pending`/`placeholder` full-bootstrap digest literals cannot be used
  for artifact, proof-key pair, or key-material commitments. This closes the gap
  where a shape-valid material record could carry recognizable placeholder
  digests until concrete artifact validation ran later.

  placeholder digest denylist, so a forged evidence record cannot advertise
  pending proof-key pair or proof-key material commitments while still satisfying

## 2026-06-10 BFV release-audit artifact canonical headers

- Hardened BFV full-bootstrap release-audit package construction and validation
  so external audit reports must start with
  `iroha.crypto.fhe.bfv.full_bootstrap.release_audit_report.v1\n` and evidence
  archives must start with
  `iroha.crypto.fhe.bfv.full_bootstrap.release_audit_archive.v1\n` before their
  bytes can be hashed, signed, packaged, or accepted. Both artifact bodies must
  also be present and not all zero after the header.
- Added regressions for both builder-side rejection and manually signed package
  bypass attempts where the report/archive digest matches the signed record but
  the packaged bytes omit the canonical v1 header, contain only the header, or
  carry an all-zero body. Core's audited material and execution prover wrappers
  also now reject unheadered, header-only, zero-body, and copied-body
  release-audit artifacts before proof generation.
- Moved audit artifact max-size rejection ahead of content, header, and body
  scans, with direct small-limit coverage proving oversized zero-body and
  unheadered payloads fail on size before deeper validation.
- Added public crypto helpers that build canonical report/archive artifacts
  from externally supplied bodies by adding the v1 byte headers and rejecting
  empty or all-zero bodies before release tooling hands bytes to package
  construction. Core release-audit fixtures now use those helpers instead of
  hand-concatenating headers.
- Hardened release-audit package construction and validation so report/archive
  artifact bodies must be distinct even though their canonical headers already
  make the signed byte digests different. Builder-path and manually signed
  package regressions now reject copied report/archive bodies before release
  publication.
- Extended adversarial manifest/package coverage so stale manifest
  version/field-count values, stale manifest-authorized package version/count
  values, whitespace-padded audit scope ids, and non-approving verdicts are
  rejected through direct manifest validation, manifest digesting, package
  validation, and package digesting.
- Extended Core audited material and execution prover wrapper regressions so
  packages carrying a machine-checkable rejected manifest verdict or copied
  report/archive bodies fail through the release-audit gate before either proof
  path emits native attachments.
- Hardened the shared Core release-audit-gated material/execution wrapper
  preflight so the refresh transcript public-key digest must match the governed
  `FullBootstrapV1` bootstrap key before release-package validation or native
  proof generation continues. Material and execution wrapper regressions now
  mutate the transcript public key and assert rejection at that boundary.
- Hardened the material-native AIR proof builder with the same bounded
  transcript-domain nonce retry used by the execution-native builder, so
  repeated sampled query schedules are retried instead of failing a valid typed
  material package. The active material verifier now accepts only nonce-bound
  material domain tags derived from the statement hash and caller-bound

## 2026-06-10 BFV release audit standalone consistency gates

- Hardened BFV full-bootstrap standalone release-audit evidence validation so it
  recomputes the evaluator-artifact-set digest, full artifact-bundle digest, and
  canonical native proof-circuit fingerprint from the evidence fields before
  evidence digesting, signoff, record, or package validation can treat the audit
  as shape-valid.
- Standalone signoff payload and manifest validation now also recompute the
  canonical native proof-circuit fingerprint from their release circuit id, so a
  signed payload or machine-checkable manifest cannot advertise a stale nonzero
  native circuit fingerprint until evidence/record comparison catches it later.
- Standalone signoff payloads and manifests now also reject copied signed
  commitment fields, so external audit report/archive digests cannot alias
  artifact, proof-key, native-circuit, or other signed release commitments.
- Added regressions for stale-but-distinct evaluator-set and artifact-bundle
  digests, a matched stale prover/verifier native circuit fingerprint, and stale
  standalone signoff/manifest native circuit fingerprints plus external audit
  digest aliasing with artifact/proof-key commitments.
- Validation:
  - `cargo test -j 1 -p iroha_crypto full_bootstrap_release_audit_evidence_binds_generated_artifacts --lib -- --nocapture`
    (`1` passed, `690` filtered out)
  - `cargo fmt --package iroha_crypto -- --check`

## 2026-06-10 Sumeragi first-delivery live commit gate crossing

- Added
  `RbcDeliveryEntryCommitEvidenceBranchAlwaysMatchesLiveCommitGateCrossing` to
  the Sumeragi formal model and wired it into the fast, deep, and TLC-fast
  configs. The theorem proves that the first-delivery commit-evidence branch
  selector exactly controls the live commit gate crossing: certified delivery
  opens the post-delivery gate from the pre-delivery closed gate, while pending
  delivery keeps the gate closed with no certificate stack or commit witnesses.
- Updated the Sumeragi formal README and roadmap proof inventory for the new
  delivery-entry live commit gate crossing obligation.

  report and evidence archive payloads must be non-empty, non-all-zero, bounded
  byte artifacts whose bytes match the reviewer-signed digests. This prevents an
  internally self-consistent release package from substituting obvious
  zero-filled placeholder evidence before audited material or execution proof
  wrappers emit native BFV proof attachments.

  archive bytes fail before a release-audit package is constructed, not only
  when a manually assembled package is later validated.

  archive packages, proving both material and execution proof paths reject the
  inert audit artifacts before native BFV proof attachments are emitted.

  stale record or manifest digests, and signed all-zero report/archive packages
  now fail before any release-audit record, manifest, or caller-pinned package
  digest can be produced.

## 2026-06-10 BFV full-bootstrap proof-material artifact-aware validation

- Added an artifact-aware validator for externally held BFV full-bootstrap
  execution witness material. It first runs the existing self-consistency
  checks, then reconstructs the public claim and recomputes the deterministic
  governed prefix trace from the supplied `FullBootstrapV1` key, concrete
  artifact bundle, and Galois keys, rejecting forged prefix-stage trace
  material before release-prover input construction can rely on it.
- Added matching artifact-aware proof-input and release-prover input material
  validators: after generic package validation, they rerun the governed witness
  trace check, and the prover-input validator also decodes the prover/verifier
  key artifacts from the concrete bundle and requires the supplied package to
  match those governed bytes.
- Pinned the boundary with a regression that accepts canonical witness material
  plus canonical proof/prover input material, while rejecting an internally
  self-consistent coefficient-to-slot trace drift against the governed artifacts.

## 2026-06-10 BFV native AIR governed-material fail-closed verifier

- Tightened the Soracloud BFV-native full-bootstrap execution verifier so the
  active STARK/FRI path requires verifier-derived governed arithmetic trace rows
  and AIR composition values after native AIR boundary preflight. Boundary-valid
  native AIR without that governed material now fails closed before explicit
  row/composition Merkle and FRI replay.
- Updated native AIR regression fixtures to reconstruct the full sample trace
  used by the proof envelope, preserving lower-level public-padding boundary
  tests with lightweight contexts where those tests intentionally bypass the
  governed-material equality check.
- Added `zk-preverify` regressions proving cached full-bootstrap execution
  proof hits cannot bypass release-native BFV AIR drift rejection or replace
  the verifier-owned governed trace/composition material required for explicit
  STARK/FRI replay.
- Aligned the existing generic-AIR preverify drift regression with the active
  verifier setup so it enables the same STARK sample guardrails before asserting
  the intended drift diagnostic instead of failing at the node-disabled guard.
- Crypto-side AIR evaluation validation now recomputes the canonical
  trace-bound composition vector from the row-major arithmetic trace before
  accepting release-prover input material.
- Core proof-emitting full-bootstrap execution helpers are now internal; the
  callable production batch path goes through release-audit package validation
  before emitting native BFV/STARK proof attachments.
