## 2026-06-08 ISO notary exact schema gate

- Hardened the ISO notary audit-index replay validators in
  `scripts/iso_audit_notary_adapter.py` and
  `scripts/iso_operator_receipt_verify.py` so each `records[]` entry must carry
  the complete Torii-emitted summary key set, including nullable fields such as
  `uetr`, before adapter publication or receipt source replay can proceed.
- Hardened persisted notary record-source replay to require the complete
  Torii-emitted record, context, metadata, and status-history key sets while
  still allowing intentional JSON nulls for nullable fields.
- Aligned persisted notary record-source replay in
  `scripts/iso_audit_notary_adapter.py` and
  `scripts/iso_operator_receipt_verify.py` with Torii's 1 MiB
  persisted-record cap instead of the broader 64 MiB anchor/index JSON cap.
- Hardened notary publication plus source-file and production-evidence replay
  so zero-record anchors cannot satisfy persisted-source proof: the notary
  adapter rejects `record_count = 0` before network delivery, the receipt
  verifier rejects it when `--require-source-files` is used, the evidence gate
  rejects compact notary receipts with non-positive `record_count`, and
  readiness replays the same invariant as receipt metadata blockers.
- Hardened notary audit-index record validation so both publication and receipt
  source replay reject unsupported lifecycle states before a digest-correct
  summary can be treated as Torii-emitted evidence.
- Hardened notary audit-index record validation so both publication and receipt
  source replay reject digest-correct lifecycle/pacs.002 summary mismatches, for
  example a `Rejected` row carrying an accepting pacs.002 code.
- Hardened persisted notary status-history verification so digest-correct record
  sources cannot carry lifecycle/pacs.002 mismatches in historical entries while
  still ending with a valid current status.
- Hardened production-readiness replay of plan-only compact canary evidence:
  plan-only summaries now keep producing production blockers with
  explicitly recorded `receipt_summary = null` and empty `stage_windows`, while
  forged plan-only summaries that omit or smuggle receipt summaries, or smuggle
  execution windows, remain malformed.
- Added archived-evidence regression coverage proving the diagnostic
  `--allow-plan-only` path preserves the same compact replay shape with
  `stage_windows = []`, an explicitly present `receipt_summary = null`, and no
  direct receipt-verification archive.
- Hardened the evidence producer to reject `--allow-plan-only` unless at least
  one archived canary summary actually records `plan_only = true`, so that
  diagnostic policy bit cannot be emitted beside fully executed canary
  evidence.
- Hardened the evidence producer to reject `--allow-partial-canary` unless at
  least one archived canary summary is missing a rail or notary stage, while
  preserving the allowed rail+verify or notary+verify diagnostic path when the
  receipt archive matches the partial canary evidence.
- Hardened the evidence producer to reject unused legacy/default-profile receipt
  overrides unless compact rail receipts actually carry legacy `colr.007` or
  missing-profile evidence, and to reject unused record-only/synthetic/missing-source
  trust overrides unless compact trust summaries carry the corresponding
  diagnostic trust material.
- Hardened the direct receipt verifier to reject unused `--allow-failed`,
  `--allow-insecure-http`, `--allow-legacy-colr007`, and
  `--allow-default-profile` flags unless verified receipts actually carry failed
  status, an HTTP/local endpoint, legacy `colr.007`, or a missing rail profile.
- Hardened plan-only canary evidence so `--allow-insecure-http` is considered
  used only when a planned rail/notary command actually targets HTTP or
  local/private routing, and `--allow-failed-receipts` requires receipt summary
  evidence with at least one failed receipt entry instead of planned command text
  or a summary flag alone, preventing standalone planned flags from satisfying
  production evidence overrides.
- Hardened production-readiness replay of compact receipt evidence so forged
  failed-receipt, legacy `colr.007`, or default-profile policy flags with no
  matching receipt entries now emit explicit diagnostic-policy blockers instead
  of looking like real local-policy allowances.
- Hardened the trust-bundle preflight to reject unused local-audit
  `--allow-record-only`, `--allow-insecure-source-url`, and
  `--allow-synthetic-der` flags unless verified bundle content actually carries
  matching non-production policy, `http://` source provenance, or synthetic DER
  evidence. The private synthetic-DER usage marker is stripped before trust
  summaries are emitted.
- Hardened evidence and readiness replay of compact trust summaries so forged
  `allow_record_only` or `allow_insecure_source_url` flags now require matching
  compact material: a non-production `embedded_signature_policy` or an
  `http://`/local/private source URL.
- Added archived-evidence regression coverage proving non-emitted trust
  profile JSON must still record `profile_json_sha256 = null`; omitting the
  field is malformed rather than an inferred diagnostic absence.
- Added readiness replay coverage for the same non-emitted trust profile JSON
  contract, so digest-correct compact evidence that omits `profile_json_sha256`
  or smuggles a non-null digest is rejected before blocker reporting.
- Hardened readiness replay of canary-stage-only diagnostic evidence so
  `receipt_verification = null` is accepted under the local override only when
  the archived evidence policy also records
  `allow_canary_stage_receipts_only = true`; digest-correct summaries that forge
  that policy back to production while skipping direct receipt archive
  verification now remain blocked.
- Tightened that diagnostic exception further: if direct receipt archive
  verification is present, a digest-correct summary that still carries
  `allow_canary_stage_receipts_only = true` remains blocked even when the local
  readiness override is supplied.
- Hardened the evidence producer to reject
  `--allow-canary-stage-receipts-only` whenever direct `--receipt` or
  `--receipt-dir` archive inputs are supplied, so the non-production policy bit
  cannot be emitted alongside direct receipt archive verification.
- Hardened the evidence producer to reject
  `--allow-profile-json-not-emitted` unless at least one archived trust summary
  actually records `profile_json_emitted = false`, so the diagnostic policy bit
  cannot be emitted beside otherwise complete profile-JSON evidence.
- Hardened the ISO operator canary runner so any executed rail, notary, or
  receipt-verify stage with truncated stdout/stderr previews or non-empty
  successful stderr now marks the canary summary failed even when the child
  process exits with status `0`. This prevents incomplete or warning-bearing
  child output, including receipt-verifier output, from becoming successful
  production evidence.
- Hardened the live ISO rail and notary adapters so 2xx responses containing
  secret-looking or unsafe control-bearing response bodies fail before any
  successful receipt is written. Failed upstream responses still redact
  secret-looking or unsafe control-bearing response previews and errors for
  diagnostics.
- Hardened live adapter local override handling so rail rejects unused
  `--allow-insecure-http`, `--allow-default-profile`, and
  `--allow-legacy-colr007`, and notary rejects unused `--allow-insecure-http`,
  unless the validated URL or sidecars actually require the corresponding local
  diagnostic policy. The notary adapter also rejects unused
  `--allow-missing-record-sources` unless at least one validated anchor actually
  lacks local record sources. The checks run before dry-run summaries or network
  delivery.
- Hardened receipt archive replay so successful 2xx receipts cannot carry the
  redacted response-body marker, preventing forged or legacy success receipts
  from hiding secret-looking upstream output behind a redaction sentinel.
- Hardened receipt-summary compaction so every compact receipt entry carries
  `response_body_sha256`; evidence and readiness now require that digest and
  bind direct archive receipts to canary receipt summaries across response-body
  digest drift as well as status and kind-specific metadata.
- Hardened direct receipt archive verification in the evidence gate so a
  successful child verifier must emit no stderr; ordinary warnings fail closed,
  and secret-looking or control-bearing stderr is redacted before the
  diagnostic is reported.
- Hardened optional XSD fixture validation so successful `xmllint` output must
  be empty or the normal `<fixture> validates` line. Warning-bearing success
  output now fails closed, and secret-looking or control-bearing validator
  output is redacted before the diagnostic is reported.
- Hardened Torii durable-store reload so digest-correct local persisted record
  JSON must retain the complete record, context, metadata, and status-history
  schema, including nullable fields and a non-empty status history, before the
  record can rebuild runtime status or regenerated audit indexes.
- Bound Torii durable-store reload to the digest-addressed record filename, so
  a digest-correct record whose on-disk filename no longer matches its embedded
  `message_id` is ignored and excluded from regenerated audit indexes.
- Hardened Torii durable-store reload to require the `messages` directory and
  each loaded record entry to be non-symlinked regular filesystem objects, so
  symlinked record paths or symlinked record directories are not followed while
  rebuilding runtime status.
- Hardened Torii durable-store writes to require real final directories for
  `messages`, local audit indexes, external audit export roots, and
  digest-addressed external anchor directories, preventing record, index, or
  notary preimage writes through symlinked durable-output directories.
- Added a 1 MiB persisted-record cap before JSON parsing and before writing
  durable record files or audit-index entries, so oversized digest-correct local
  records cannot rebuild runtime status and runtime-generated oversized status
  records cannot leave stale durable state.
- Aligned Torii durable-store reload with the offline source verifiers'
  clean-string policy: concrete persisted strings must be non-empty, unpadded,
  and control-free while JSON null remains valid for nullable fields.
- Added adversarial coverage for digest-correct audit indexes and persisted
  record sources that omit nullable schema keys, both directly through the
  notary adapter and through receipt-verifier notary source replay.
- Added Torii adversarial coverage for digest-correct persisted records with
  missing top-level fields, missing nested context/metadata/history fields,
  extra fields, empty status history, malformed change-reason arrays, embedded
  `message_id` drift, digest-addressed filename drift, and symlinked record
  paths, symlinked `messages` directories, plus oversized digest-correct local
  records, dirty persisted strings, and symlinked durable-output directories on
  the persist/export side.
- Updated the ISO roadmap/backlog/audit notes to describe the complete notary
  audit/source schema requirements, the split notary source caps, and the
  positive notary `record_count` requirement, state-compatible pacs.002
  summary/status-history code requirement before publication and during
  source-file or production-evidence replay, canary producer failure on
  truncated child stdout/stderr previews or successful child stderr,
  successful-response rejection for secret-looking or control-bearing
  rail/notary upstream bodies,
  unused live adapter local override rejection,
  unused local trust-bundle override rejection,
  compact receipt response-body digest binding, and successful direct
  receipt-verifier stderr rejection, plus successful `xmllint` output
  allowlisting and control-character redaction for validator and direct
  receipt-verifier diagnostics.
  Remaining production blockers are
  unchanged: real live rail/notary evidence, official trust/revocation bundles,
  and redistributable official schema/profile coverage still need operator or
  upstream inputs.
- Full dependency clippy for `iroha_torii` currently stops in unrelated
  `iroha_data_model::zk::OpenVerifyEnvelopeBounds` on
  `clippy::struct_excessive_bools`; the Torii-local `--no-deps` clippy pass

- The ISO Python/docs hygiene checks below pass and this ISO pass did not

## 2026-06-07 Kagemusha recursive compact projection boundary

- Added a data-model constructor for recursive compact token projections so a
  folded mode-2 public-input projection and recursive proof produce a canonical
  `KagemushaCompactPaymentToken` without routing through the legacy
  checked-prefold compact-token validator.
- Added recursive spend accumulator projection helpers and a validated
  recursive spend bundle-to-compact-token conversion. This gives the multi-hop
  Reserved-lineage append path a canonical chain-visible compact token shape
  while the ABI-7 compact prover still keeps multi-hop proof composition
  reserved.
- Wired the core one-hop ABI-7 compact prover and test helper through the new
  constructor so generated compact tokens and projection tests share the same
  binding checks.
- Validation:
  - `cargo fmt --all --check`
  - `cargo test -p iroha_data_model kagemusha_recursive_aggregation_evidence_binds_batch_preflight_digest -- --test-threads=1`
    (`1` test passed)
  - `cargo test -p iroha_data_model kagemusha_recursive_spend_bundle_roundtrips_and_appends_without_prior_hops -- --test-threads=1`
    (`1` test passed)
  - `cargo test -p iroha_core kagemusha_recursive_compact_payment_token_preverify_binds_token_shape --no-run`
  - The runtime `iroha_core`
    `kagemusha_recursive_compact_payment_token_preverify_binds_token_shape`
    test was interrupted after successful compilation because it entered the
    expensive recursive verifier-key materialization path.

## 2026-06-07 Kagemusha production release-bundle verifier

- Added `scripts/kagemusha_release_bundle.py` as a strict final packaging gate
  for Kagemusha production evidence. It accepts only a ready
  `dist/kagemusha-production-readiness.json`, recomputes the Reserved-lineage
  proof evidence, ABI-7 compact key evidence, and Android device-lab signed
  evidence checks, then emits
  `dist/kagemusha-production-release-bundle.json` with bundle-relative paths and
  SHA-256 bindings.
- The verifier rejects blocked or drifted readiness summaries, duplicate JSON
  keys, unexpected top-level summary fields, secret-looking paths, evidence
  outside `--bundle-root`, missing trusted signer keys, secret-looking strings
  anywhere inside the readiness summary, symlinked bundle roots, and symlinked
  or hardlinked release-bundle outputs. Secret-looking trusted signer key paths
  are rejected before key loading, and newly-created output parents are
  revalidated before writing.
- Added positive and adversarial release-bundle coverage to the Kagemusha
  readiness test suite, and pinned the new script, tests, docs, workflow path,
  and summary-drift negative control in the production-readiness source guard.
- This closes another release-packaging gap, but the release still needs actual
  generated compact key artifacts/evidence plus signed physical Android
  device-lab evidence before the bundle can be produced as ready. ABI-7
  multi-hop compact remains reserved until append-batch composition is wired.
- Cargo/Rust validation was deferred because another `cargo test -p iroha_core`
  process was active and must not be interrupted or contended with.

## 2026-06-07 Native asset-lock ISIs

- Added first-class native asset-lock instructions for escrow-style conditional
  custody: `OpenAssetLock`, `DrawdownAssetLock`, `CancelAssetLock`, and
  `ExpireAssetLock`.
- Generic locks now record their behavior kind, remaining amount, optional
  release authority, optional expiry deadline, and terminal `DrawnDown` or
  `Expired` status. Existing marketplace escrows are marked separately as
  `Marketplace` records.
- Lock funding moves source balances into deterministic native custody, and
  generic asset transfer or burn instructions cannot drain recorded native
  escrow custody accounts. Drawdown, cancellation, and expiry use the native
  escrow custody policy instead.

  finite positive amount validation before transaction construction.
- Added unit, SDK-surface, and 4-peer localnet coverage for duplicate IDs,
  missing accounts, non-positive amounts, insufficient balance, wrong kind,
  wrong signer, release authority checks, overdraw, frozen custody, expiry
  timing, closed-state replays, and direct custody-drain attempts.

## 2026-06-07 ISO XSD source repository placeholder gate

- Hardened `scripts/iso_xsd_fixture_verify.py` so checked-in XSD schema source
  provenance and blocked public candidate-source provenance share the same
  canonical GitHub repository validator.
- Source repository coordinates now reject placeholder owners or repository
  names such as `example`, `dummy`, `fake`, `sample`, `template`, `test`,
  `replace-before-production`, and `operator-canary.bank` forms, in addition
  to the existing canonical URL, no-`.git`, length, commit, path, digest, and
  restricted-terms checks.
- Mirrored the repository-coordinate predicate in
  `scripts/iso_production_readiness.py` so digest-correct archived XSD summaries
  cannot bypass the direct manifest preflight by replaying placeholder schema
  source or blocked candidate-source metadata into the aggregate release gate.
  Readiness now also rejects secret-looking archived XSD repository coordinates
  before normalized summary output can echo them.
- Tightened direct XSD manifest schema paths, fixture paths, and source
  provenance paths so identifier-style secret material such as
  `token-...-secret` is rejected before summary emission, matching the
  readiness replay and output-path guards.
- Updated the XSD verifier tests so valid offline fixtures use real public
  source coordinates and added adversarial owner/name placeholder regressions
  for both checked-in schema sources and blocked candidate-source evidence,
  including forged readiness-summary replay and identifier-style source/path
  no-echo cases. Direct XSD preflight now also has explicit no-echo coverage for
  secret-looking checked-in schema source repositories and blocked candidate
  source repositories.
- Added a production-readiness parity regression that compares the direct XSD
  preflight, direct trust-bundle preflight, operator evidence replay, and final
  readiness replay predicates for placeholder XSD repositories and trust-source
  metadata, plus the rail, notary, canary, receipt, and evidence endpoint-host
  predicates for reserved documentation hosts and checked-in template canary
  hosts, so future local hardening cannot update only one layer.
- Added a second production-readiness parity regression that pins the required
  receipt-kind set, receipt suffix, profile/message-type regexes, supported
  rail message-type allowlist, legacy `colr.007` classification, and
  `colr.012` production endpoint coverage across the direct rail adapter,
  direct receipt verifier, operator evidence replay, and final readiness
  replay.
- Hardened direct receipt verification, operator evidence replay, and final
  readiness replay so rail receipt metadata with a syntactically valid but
  unsupported `message_type` such as `zzzz.999` is rejected before forged
  summaries can satisfy production evidence.
- Hardened direct receipt verification so malformed archived rail
  `message_type` family IDs such as `PACS.002` fail before the supported-type
  allowlist, while secret-looking message-type identifiers still take the
  existing no-echo secret-material diagnostic path first.
- Added a production-readiness taxonomy parity regression that pins supported
  rail/profile identifiers, profile directions, signature-policy names,
  schema-source licenses, and profile/message regexes across XSD manifest
  preflight, trust-bundle preflight, operator evidence replay, and final
  readiness replay.
- Hardened operator evidence replay and final readiness replay so unsupported
  trust `embedded_signature_policy` values such as `diagnostic-only` are
  rejected distinctly even when local record-only diagnostic replay is enabled.
- Hardened compact trust-summary replay so evidence summaries now retain the
  source trust-verifier diagnostic flags `allow_synthetic_der`,
  `allow_record_only`, and `allow_insecure_source_url`; readiness requires those
  booleans, blocks any true value as non-production evidence, and includes them
  when recomputing compact `profile_json_emittable` drift.
- Aligned local evidence diagnostic acceptance so non-emittable trust summaries
  use their matching override (`--allow-record-only-trust`,
  `--allow-insecure-http`, `--allow-synthetic-trust`, or
  `--allow-missing-trust-source`) instead of requiring the synthetic-trust
  override for record-only or insecure-source replay.
- Narrowed `--allow-missing-trust-source` so it only permits non-emittable
  profile JSON when a compact trust source is actually missing; present but
  stale-under-budget source provenance still fails closed even if the missing
  source diagnostic override is supplied.
- Hardened evidence and final readiness replay so evidence-generated compact
  trust profiles with explicit `source: null` are retained as diagnostic
  evidence and reported as `trust.source_missing` blockers, while compact
  profiles that omit the `source` key remain malformed even under
  `--allow-missing-trust-source`.
- Hardened final readiness replay so `receipt_verification` must be present in
  every evidence summary; explicit `null` remains the recorded canary-stage-only
  diagnostic shape, while omitting the key is malformed even when local
  canary-stage-only replay is allowed.
- Hardened operator evidence replay so `--allow-dry-run`,
  `--allow-failed-receipts`, and `--allow-insecure-http` are rejected when no
  archived canary command, receipt summary, or trust summary actually carries the
  corresponding diagnostic policy. The archived evidence JSON keeps those
  producer-only markers internal, so compact canary summaries do not grow new
  underscore fields.
- Bound canary verify-stage receipt-verifier command flags to the captured
  receipt-verifier JSON policy booleans for failed receipts, insecure HTTP,
  legacy `colr.007`, default-profile fallback, and required source files. The
  canary receipt replay now also validates legacy rail metadata against the
  child receipt summary's recorded `allow_legacy_colr007` policy instead of the
  top-level local override.
- Hardened final readiness replay so local `--allow-reviewed-xsd-gaps` and
  `--allow-canary-stage-receipts-only` overrides are rejected when no reviewed
  XSD warning or canary-stage-only receipt evidence actually needs them. The
  internal replay marker for archived canary-stage-only policy is stripped from
  the public readiness summary before digesting.

## 2026-06-07 ISO trust-source template and reserved host gate

- Hardened trust-bundle production source checks so `dummy`, `fake`, `sample`,
  and `template` authority/version metadata are treated as placeholder
  provenance alongside `placeholder`, `replace-before-production`, and reserved
  source hosts such as `.example`, `example.com`, `example.net`, `example.org`,
  `example.invalid`, and `operator-canary.bank`.
- Applied the predicate consistently in `scripts/iso_trust_bundle_verify.py`,
  `scripts/iso_operator_evidence_verify.py`, and
  `scripts/iso_production_readiness.py`, so generated summaries, archived
  evidence replay, and aggregate readiness all refuse profile-emittable
  production evidence that still carries template wording.
- Added adversarial coverage for summary-only trust verification, profile JSON
  emission refusal, evidence replay, and compact readiness replay, including
  text markers, reserved documentation-domain hosts, and checked-in canary
  template hosts used as forged trust-source provenance.
- Archived canary child command endpoint replay now rejects reserved
  documentation-domain hosts before a forged template-host canary summary can
  satisfy production evidence verification. That rejection is unconditional for
  reserved/template hosts, including under local `--allow-insecure-http`
  diagnostic replay.
- Direct rail/notary receipt endpoint verification now applies the same
  reserved placeholder-host rejection, including `.example`, plus checked-in
  `operator-canary.bank` template-host rejection after structural URL checks so
  documentation-only or template endpoints cannot satisfy production receipt
  evidence. Direct evidence archive verification inherits the same receipt
  endpoint gate before accepting archived rail/notary receipts.
- Live rail gateway, audit notary, and canary runbook endpoint validation now
  apply the same reserved placeholder-host rejection before planning or network
  delivery. Direct rail gateway and audit notary adapter invocations also reject
  checked-in `operator-canary.bank` template hosts before network delivery. The
  checked-in operator canary templates now use non-reserved
  `operator-canary.bank` endpoints so template planning still exercises the
  runbooks without relying on documentation-only hosts; non-plan canary runs
  reject that template suffix before child execution, and archived production
  evidence separately rejects it before accepting child-command endpoint replay.

  `scripts/iso_production_readiness.py` so blocked public XSD candidate evidence
  must include at least one explicit redistribution or public-distribution

## 2026-06-07 Kagemusha Swift native output pre-copy cap

- Swift's Darwin `NoritoNativeBridge` now routes compact-token, recursive
  aggregation, recursive compact, recursive spend, and lineage-witness
  Kagemusha native outputs through a shared checked copier.
- The copier rejects declared native output lengths above
  `KagemushaRecursiveSpendProver.nativeArchiveMaxBytes` before constructing
  `Data`, and still frees the native pointer on both bounded-copy success and
  over-cap rejection.
- Added Swift pointer-level tests plus SDK parity and JS meta-test markers so
  Kagemusha Swift output paths cannot drift back to direct `Data(bytes:)`
  copies; the SDK parity guard now has a negative control that weakens both the
  bridge cap and oversized-output test name to prove that drift is detected.

## 2026-06-07 WSL cargo-test root-cause reduction

- Removed the default debug-symbol load from local dev/test builds by setting
  `profile.dev.debug=0` and `profile.test.debug=0`; developers can still opt in
  with `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=line-tables-only` or
  `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=line-tables-only` when actively debugging.
- Kept long plain `cargo test` runs conservative by default:
  `build.jobs=1`, `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1`, and `profile.test.incremental=false`
  prevent WSL from stacking multiple high-RSS `rustc` processes, libtest
  thread fans, and incremental-query cache growth.
- Disabled Cargo's automatic one-file-one-binary integration-test discovery for
  the highest-count crates and replaced it with explicit grouped harnesses:
  `ivm`, `norito`, `iroha_core`, `iroha_data_model`, `iroha_crypto`, and
  `iroha_torii`. The six crates now expose `32` test targets instead of `805`,
  while grouped coverage accounts for `797` intended scenario files with only
  explicit feature-gated targets and fixture/helper files excluded.
- Hardened `scripts/run_full_tests.sh --wsl-safe` so the fast workspace suite
  runs one package at a time, sets `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, serializes network
  tests, checks `/proc/meminfo` `MemAvailable` before each Cargo step, and
  writes memory/cgroup/disk/top-RSS snapshots to
  `<target-dir>/run_full_tests_resources.log` by default.
- Remaining known hotspot: `iroha_data_model` still peaks around `10 GiB` RSS
  as a single stripped-debuginfo Rust compile on this WSL host. The current
  fix prevents that peak from being multiplied by Cargo parallelism and
  duplicate integration-test linking; further reduction requires splitting or
  simplifying the data-model compile surface.
- Validation:
  - `cargo fmt --all`
  - `bash -n scripts/run_full_tests.sh`
  - `scripts/run_full_tests.sh --help`
  - `scripts/run_full_tests.sh --wsl-safe --target-dir /tmp/iroha-run-full-tests-wsl-guard-check --min-available-mib 999999`
    (exited `75` before starting `cargo build --workspace`)
  - `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 | python3 -c '...'`
    (`ivm=10`, `norito=6`, `iroha_core=6`, `iroha_data_model=3`,
    `iroha_crypto=1`, `iroha_torii=6` test targets)
  - Grouped coverage audit:
    `ivm 303/303`, `norito 169/169`, `iroha_core 138/138`,
    `iroha_data_model 60/60`, `iroha_crypto 32/32`, `iroha_torii 95/95`
  - `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo test -p norito --tests --no-run`
  - `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo test -p iroha_crypto --tests --no-run`
  - `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo test -p iroha_data_model --tests --no-run`
  - `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo test -p ivm --tests --no-run`
  - `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo test -p iroha_core --tests --no-run`
  - `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo test -p iroha_torii --tests --no-run`

## 2026-06-07 Soracloud full-bootstrap execution proof gate

- Added the canonical Soracloud BFV full-bootstrap execution proof envelope,
  public-input schema, OpenVerify bounds, and validation rules to the data
  model. Proof attachments must bind the canonical full-bootstrap circuit id,
  STARK/Fri backend, statement hash, verifier-key commitment, and envelope hash.
- Extended `RunSoracloudFheJob`, Torii job-run payloads, and signed provenance
  with an ordered full-bootstrap execution-proof vector, so proof
  insertion/removal is covered by the authority signature.
- Wired Core full-bootstrap jobs to require one execution proof per output slot
  after artifact-aware exact/bounded execution. Core derives each statement from
  the governed public key, full-bootstrap key/material, artifact bundle,
  input/output ciphertexts, bound mode, and input/output bounds; it then checks
  the active Soracloud verifier-key record against the governed verifier-key
  artifact before backend verification.
- Added a `zk-preverify` positive regression that installs the governed
  full-bootstrap verifier key, preloads the block-level preverified-proof cache
  for every output-slot proof, asserts the default confidential verifier-call
  quota admits at least one 64-slot Soracloud identifier proof batch, and proves
  the Core verifier gate accepts the preverified active verifier path while
  default tests still reject missing, surplus, reordered, metadata-drifted,
  statement-drifted, and unverified fake proofs.
- Confirmed the default confidential per-transaction verifier-call cap is `128`,
  with the per-block cap also at `128`, so a first-run configuration admits one
  production-shaped Soracloud BFV full-bootstrap execution proof batch without
  an operator override.
- Cleared current `iroha_config --tests` clippy blockers in SCCP route-manifest
  helpers while validating the default change under `-D warnings`.

## 2026-06-07 SCCP Groth16 proof-request source bundle gate

- Hardened Rust EVM/TRON Groth16 UI proof-request construction and proof-result
  wrapping so request `bundle_bytes` must decode as canonical SCCP message
  bundle bytes, match the transparent public inputs, and carry non-empty
  source-proof witness bytes whenever the bundle source domain is not SORA.
- Restored the SCCP launch-scope note: current SCCP support remains limited to
  Ethereum, BSC, Solana, TON, and TRON; retired runtime-network families remain
  outside the production surface.
- Added an explicit note that retired runtime-network families remain outside
  SCCP launch support for now.
- Added EVM and TRON negative/adversarial regressions for omitted source-proof

## 2026-06-07 Soracloud full-bootstrap execution proof runtime metadata guard

- Added a Core runtime adversarial regression for full-bootstrap execution
  proofs. It verifies that missing `vk_commitment`, forged verifier-key
  commitment, missing `envelope_hash`, and forged proof-byte envelope hashes are
  rejected during runtime admission before verifier lookup can mask attachment
  metadata drift.
- Extended the Core proof-vector regression to reject surplus full-bootstrap
  execution proofs and per-slot proof reordering before any backend verifier
  can accept a proof for the wrong output slot.
- Extended the Core proof-vector regression to reject bound-mode replay in both
  directions. Exact-residual proofs are rejected under bounded-noise admission,
  and bounded-noise proofs are rejected under exact-residual admission before
  verifier lookup.
- Added a data-model regression that keeps the expected execution statement hash
  present but reshapes STARK public inputs with extra rows, extra columns, or a
  duplicate statement. Full-bootstrap execution proof attachments must still
  reject those wrappers before runtime admission.
- Added Torii signed job-run preflight for verifier-backed FHE proof
  attachments. A replay-shaped but correctly signed execution proof attachment
  now fails locally as a bad request before instruction construction.
- Fixed the Core bootstrap-key proof backend verifier path to decode proof
  attachments with the bootstrap-key context instead of the full-material
  context, restoring the dedicated label and size-cap surface for that proof
  class.

## 2026-06-07 SCCP source-adapter proof-body checked writer

- Added a fallible canonical source-adapter proof-body writer for the checked
  SCCP encoder path. The checked path now uses explicit `u32` length-prefix
  writes for nested proof vectors, list counts, source-state proof capsules,
  validator/signature rosters, Solana account openings, TON config proofs, and
  TRON header/receipt/transaction branches instead of delegating back to the
  panic-only legacy encoder after shape preflight.
- Added cross-lane checked-encoder tests for Ethereum, BSC, Solana, TON, and
  TRON that require byte-for-byte compatibility with legacy canonical
  transcripts and reject lane-specific oversized proof-body shapes through both
  checked byte encoding and checked proof hashing.
- The checked FastPQ context now rejects unknown source domains instead of
  normalizing the missing chain key to an empty string. A regression covers the
  checked context writer and `build_sccp_source_adapter_fastpq_batch`.
- Removed mechanically duplicated Soracloud full-bootstrap execution proof
  constants/OpenVerify helpers in `iroha_data_model` that blocked SCCP test
  compilation before `iroha_sccp` could run.
- Validation:
  - `cargo fmt -p iroha_sccp -p iroha_data_model`
  - `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/iroha-codex-sccp-proof-body-len CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -j 1 -p iroha_sccp sccp_checked --lib -- --nocapture`

## 2026-06-07 BFV full-bootstrap executable sample-switch prefix trace

- Added a governed full-bootstrap prefix trace that validates concrete artifact
  bundles and executes coefficient-to-slot, blind-rotation, and raw
  sample-extraction stages through exact and bounded registered RNS paths, then
  feeds the coefficient-zero diagnostic repack through the governed
  slot-to-coefficient transform.
- Added deterministic exact and bounded raw-sample switch-key material,
  owner-side secret-consistency checks, exact/bounded switch execution, and
  public bound propagation for switching extracted samples into
  coefficient-zero BFV ciphertexts.
- Added artifact-aware final-output entry points for exact and bounded paths
  that execute the governed prefix or prefix-bound propagation through
  sample-switch and slot-to-coefficient output.
- Threaded signed full-bootstrap artifact bundles through the Core Soracloud
  runtime bound and execution helpers so exact/bounded full-mode jobs invoke the
  artifact-aware crypto output path instead of only doing standalone artifact
  preflight.
- Restricted the legacy no-artifact Core execution helpers to unit tests; the
  production Soracloud runtime now reaches full-bootstrap execution only through
  the artifact-aware helper path that rejects missing governed artifacts before
  bound propagation or ciphertext evaluation.
- The artifact-aware final APIs now consume governed sample switch-key artifacts
  and return the slot-to-coefficient output/bound for exact and bounded paths.
- Direct crypto no-artifact registered entrypoints now validate the same
  public full-bootstrap preflight, then fail with an explicit governed-artifact
  requirement instead of the stale unavailable-evaluator error. Remaining work
  is proof-checked artifact dispatch with the real prover/verifier backend.
- Added exact/bounded regressions proving the prefix trace matches stage
  baselines, the raw sample decrypts to the selected blind-rotation coefficient,
  sample switch keys preserve only coefficient-zero plaintext, propagated bounds
  cover each stage, valid artifact-aware final calls return the governed
  slot-to-coefficient output/bound, and missing Galois keys fail closed.

  transforms and for the executable full-bootstrap prefix trace. The prefix
  helper validates the governed `FullBootstrapV1` key and artifact bundle, then
  composes coefficient-to-slot, blind-rotation, and raw sample-extraction bounds
  for the same artifacts consumed by prefix execution.
- Extended the prefix trace regression so exact and bounded execution validate
  coefficient-to-slot outputs, blind-rotation outputs, and raw extracted samples
  against propagated bounds, verify the diagnostic coefficient-zero repack
  output, use bounded refresh material on the bounded path, and fail closed
  when required Galois material is missing.
- Added an explicit coefficient-zero raw-sample repack diagnostic bridge. It
  proves the extracted raw sample can be represented in the RLWE ring at
  coefficient zero with exact and bounded coefficient-zero bounds, and the
  executable prefix trace now carries that diagnostic ciphertext while keeping
  the final full-ciphertext sample key-switch/repacking stage unavailable.
- Superseded by the later sample-switch entry: direct no-artifact registered
  entrypoints now fail closed with an explicit governed-artifact requirement;
  remaining work is proof-checked full-bootstrap verification and the real
  prover/verifier backend.

## 2026-06-07 BFV full-bootstrap raw sample extraction

- Added `BfvFullBootstrapRawExtractedSampleV1` plus exact and bounded raw
  sample-extraction helpers and matching output-bound helpers. The primitive
  extracts the selected RLWE coefficient into an LWE-style sample aligned with
  `BfvSecretKey::s`, preserving the negacyclic sign convention instead of
  pretending the current artifact can already key-switch or repack into a normal
  two-component BFV ciphertext.
- Added owner-side scaled decrypt and exact/bounded profile helpers for raw
  extracted samples, then covered them with a regression that compares the raw
  sample decrypt against the selected source BFV decrypt coefficient for both
  exact and bounded-noise ciphertexts, and asserts the propagated raw sample
  bounds cover the resulting owner-side profiles.
- Remaining work: key-switch/repack the raw extracted sample into the governed
  output ciphertext shape, wire the stage into the full-bootstrap evaluator, and
  replace typed placeholder proof-profile material with the real prover/verifier
  backend.

## 2026-06-07 Sumeragi committed spec-step stutter/GST closure

- Added `CommittedSpecStepStuttersOrObservesGstStep` /
  `CommittedSpecStepStuttersOrObservesGst` to the top-level Sumeragi model so
  committed-state spec behavior is checked as a complete stutter/GST split.
- The property combines the pre-GST `[Next]_vars` split, the committed+GST
  terminal stuttering theorem, and the non-stuttering GST-observation
  exclusivity theorem: after finality, spec steps either stutter in the current
  committed state or take `GstElapsed` into committed+GST terminal quiescence.
- Wired the property through `Sumeragi_fast.cfg`, `Sumeragi_deep.cfg`, and
  `Sumeragi_tlc_fast.cfg`, and documented the committed spec-step closure
  obligation in the formal README and roadmap.

## 2026-06-07 RBC DELIVER quorum hardening

- Tightened inbound RBC DELIVER acceptance so a valid external DELIVER no
  longer marks a chunk-complete RBC-only session delivered before READY quorum
  is present. The existing local authoritative-payload shortcut remains scoped
  to pending, in-flight, or committed block payloads, not merely reconstructed
  RBC chunks.
- Hardened the `sumeragi.debug.rbc.force_deliver_quorum_one` boundary: the
  override can still lower local DELIVER emission in adversarial/throughput
  harnesses, but inbound DELIVER acceptance always uses the protocol quorum and
  deferred inbound DELIVERs no longer trigger same-turn local delivery.
- Added an adversarial handler regression proving a single signed DELIVER with
  no READY bundle is deferred for a complete metadata-bound RBC payload, added a
  debug-override regression proving one external READY bundle entry is still
  deferred until protocol quorum, and updated the complete-RS16 telemetry
  regression to use a real signed READY quorum before asserting payload-byte
  accounting.

  operator-script, and public-documentation paths. Public SCCP discovery,
  manifests, launch readiness, and SDK helpers now stay limited to Ethereum,
  BSC, Solana, TON, and TRON.

  surfaces so public names, generated declarations, and package artifacts fail
  if the removed lane token is reintroduced.

  itself, including a negative stale-allowance marker check and evidence-phase
  transcript coverage for the guard test.
- Corrected the retired-network scan's Kotlin SDK test root to the real
  `src/test/kotlin` package and added a root-existence/nonempty guard so
  missing scan roots cannot silently shrink coverage.
- Removed the obsolete retired runtime-network lane material from the
  `docs/source/new_pipeline*.md` pipeline docs and translations, and extended
  the retired-network scan to cover those files so translated docs cannot
  reintroduce the lane. The guard now asserts every translated
  `new_pipeline*.md` document is included in the scan set.

  retired-network guard without the translated pipeline-doc coverage marker and
  requires the strict inventory check to report the missing guard.

  release-readiness tests, so readiness and bundle verification both fail if

## 2026-06-07 BFV full-bootstrap blind-rotation artifact validation

- Added typed `BfvFullBootstrapBlindRotationStepV1` and
  `BfvFullBootstrapBlindRotationKeyV1` payloads for governed full-bootstrap
  blind-rotation artifacts. The key binds the target slot count, accumulator
  artifact digest, packed-left-rotation amount, and canonical Galois
  automorphism selector plaintext schedule.
- Full-bootstrap artifact bundle admission now decodes and validates typed
  blind-rotation bytes instead of accepting opaque role/profile envelopes. The
  validator rejects zero or mismatched accumulator digests, duplicate
  automorphism powers, malformed selector plaintexts, non-binary selectors, and
  schedules that do not match the deterministic packed-slot rotation surface.
- Core and data-model sample artifact helpers now construct blind-rotation
  artifacts from the same typed accumulator artifact digest used by governed
  material commitments. The sample-extraction artifact API now passes the
  scalar `Copy` payload by value to satisfy the strict clippy pass-by-reference
  lint.

## 2026-06-07 Kura/WSV benchmark coverage closure

- Added source-level closure for the remaining Kura/WSV audit perf gaps:
  `bench_eviction_helpers_seed_remote_eviction` seeds persisted Kura history,
  advertises remote replicas, and proves the bench-only eviction helpers free
  the expected body bytes; `kura_eviction_long_history_compaction` benchmarks
  long-history compaction over 64 and 512 evictable bodies.
- Added `kura_background_eviction_retry_latency_threshold`, which starts the
  Kura writer, schedules storage-budget eviction from an over-budget retry
  block, waits for writer maintenance to evict the replicated body through the
  DA sidecar path, and asserts retry completion stays under a conservative
  two-second threshold for the small regression history.
- Added `commit_heavy_world_accounts_for_bench`,
  `heavy_world_commit_bench_helper_commits_accounts`, and the

## 2026-06-07 BFV full-bootstrap typed artifact envelopes

- Added `BfvFullBootstrapCircuitArtifactRoleV1` and
  `BfvFullBootstrapCircuitArtifactPayloadV1`, plus a Norito encoder helper, so
  each full-bootstrap artifact byte field now declares its role, canonical
  circuit id, registered BFV parameter digest, RNS/decomposition digests, and
  max bootstrap depth before validation accepts it.

## 2026-06-07 WSV state write lock separation

- Replaced commit-path use of the coarse `view_lock` with a dedicated
  `state_write_lock` for multi-component writer serialization. Block commit,
  merge-ledger commit, and lane lifecycle updates now serialize writers without
  occupying a reader/writer view lock during heavy world, transaction, topology,
  and block-hash commits.
- Kept full `State::view` consistency on the existing even/odd generation
  guard, so full views still retry while a writer is active and writer-vs-writer
  ordering remains explicit.
- Updated the lock-order regressions to block on `state_write_lock` and prove
  block commit still does not hold the tiered backend while waiting for writer
  serialization.
- Refreshed the Kura/WSV audit so the WSV `view_lock` high finding is marked
  addressed; the audit currently has zero open critical/high/medium/low items.
- Validation:
  - `rustfmt --edition 2024 crates/iroha_core/src/state.rs`

## 2026-06-07 Kura background storage-budget eviction

- Changed Kura storage-budget checks to fail fast and schedule background
  block-body eviction instead of running `evict_block_bodies` on the caller
  path. Over-budget enqueue and top-replacement checks now coalesce the needed
  reclaim bytes into a pending maintenance request, wake the Kura writer, and
  return `StorageBudgetExceeded` until maintenance actually frees space.
- Added the writer-loop maintenance drain for pending storage-budget eviction
  requests. The existing compaction path remains the single reclaim
  implementation, now reached from background maintenance for budget pressure.
- Updated the budget regression so it proves the first over-budget store leaves
  the old body inline, wakes maintenance, background eviction creates the DA
  sidecar, and a retry succeeds after reclamation.
- Refreshed the Kura/WSV audit so inline foreground Kura eviction is marked
  addressed; the follow-up WSV state-write-lock entry closes the final open
  WSV commit-lock item.

## 2026-06-07 Kura eviction block-store lock split

- Split `evict_block_bodies` so it snapshots durable block-store metadata under
  `block_store`, releases that mutex while copying DA sidecars and compacting
  `blocks.data`/`blocks.index` into temp files, then reacquires `block_store`
  only for final count validation, atomic replacement, directory sync, and
  cache refresh.
- Added `block_store_write_lock` to serialize block-store mutations across
  eviction, appends, prunes, rehydration, and active path retargeting while
  allowing metadata readers to acquire `block_store` during long compaction.
- Refreshed the Kura/WSV audit so the full-rewrite-under-`block_store` high
  finding is marked addressed; foreground inline eviction remains tracked as
  the open medium item.

## 2026-06-07 Soracloud full-bootstrap material proof envelope

- Added the data-model `SoracloudFheFullBootstrapMaterialProofV1` attachment
  surface for governed `FullBootstrapV1` material statements, with canonical
  STARK/FRI backend validation, verifier-key id binding, verifier-key
  commitment binding, envelope-hash binding, and an exported schema-hash helper
  for the full-bootstrap material public-input layout.
- Added Soracloud-specific `OpenVerifyEnvelope` bounds for full-bootstrap
  material proofs and validation that rejects malformed envelopes, wrong
  circuit/schema metadata, mismatched statement public inputs, empty native
  STARK envelopes, and oversized outer/wrapper/native proof payloads before
  verifier dispatch.
- Added focused coverage for canonical envelopes, required commitments,
  attachment metadata drift, OpenVerify drift, published bounds, oversized
  payloads, and canonical verifier ids. This is still only the data-model
  envelope surface; the existing Core admission path dispatches full-material
  proofs through active Soracloud verifier records and the preverified-proof
  cache, while executable full BFV bootstrapping and the real prover/verifier
  artifacts remain pending.
- Hardened `RegisterVerifyingKey`/`UpdateVerifyingKey` admission for the
  canonical full-bootstrap material verifier profile, matching the existing
  bootstrap-key profile guard: id name/backend, namespace, STARK backend,
  Goldilocks field, circuit id/version, public-input schema hash,
  gas-schedule id, and active inline key presence now fail at registry
  admission instead of first failing during FHE job execution.
- Exported the full-bootstrap material proof constants, attachment type, bounds
  helper, and public-input schema hash through `soracloud::prelude` so the
  public Soracloud data-model surface stays aligned with Core imports.

## 2026-06-07 BFV full-bootstrap execution policy binding

- Added `FheExecutionPolicyV1::full_bootstrap_material_proof_statement_digest`
  so bootstrap-capable Soracloud policies can bind the governed
  `FullBootstrapV1` material statement instead of the deterministic
  zero-refresh statement used by `RefreshOnlyV1`. Policy validation now rejects
  missing statement bindings, stale statement fields on zero-bootstrap
  policies, and policies that bind both statement classes.
- Wired Core refresh-transcript verification to derive the full-bootstrap
  material statement from the supplied BFV parameters, evaluation keys, and
  refresh transcript before execution. Full-bootstrap bundles now omit
  deterministic zero-refresh bootstrap transcript seeds; Core rejects missing,
  mismatched, stale, and cross-mode full-material policy bindings.
- Added negative/adversarial coverage for missing full-material statements,
  wrong statement digests, cross-mode zero-refresh/full-material policies,
  stale zero-bootstrap policies, and full-bootstrap bundles that try to carry
  deterministic zero-refresh transcript seeds.

  metadata-bound paths can evaluate.

## 2026-06-06 Kura writer wake coalescing

- Replaced the Kura writer notification channel with a capacity-one
  `sync_channel` and routed producer wakeups through non-blocking `try_send`, so
  redundant `NewBlock` wake events coalesce instead of accumulating under
  sustained producer pressure.
- Updated pipeline sidecar enqueueing to wake the writer only on an
  empty-to-nonempty transition; the sidecar queue itself is still intentionally
  tracked as an open cap/backpressure item.
- Added a regression proving consecutive pipeline sidecar enqueue calls leave
  both sidecars queued but only one writer wake pending.
- Validation:
  - `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -j 1 -p iroha_core pipeline_sidecar_enqueue_coalesces_writer_notifications --lib -- --nocapture`
    (`1` passed, `6961` filtered out)

## 2026-06-06 BFV RNS negacyclic root metadata

- Added registered primitive `2n`-th negacyclic NTT roots for the RAM-LFE BFV
  RNS modulus chain and bound them by index to the registered modulus limbs.
- Registered RNS chain admission now validates the concrete root table before
  exposing the production chain or digest, and direct chain callers can use
  `validate_negacyclic_ntt_support` to preflight root availability.
- Shared RNS chain validation now enforces bounded concrete negacyclic NTT root
  support for every validated limb, so direct callers cannot validate a chain
  that later falls back because the NTT root is unsupported.
- RNS limb multiplication now uses the registered root table for production
  limbs before falling back to deterministic root discovery for non-registered
  structural limbs.
- Generic primitive-root discovery is now candidate-bounded, so unsupported
  caller-supplied RNS or packed-slot primes fall back or fail closed instead of
  scanning unbounded candidate ranges.
- The RNS chain now exposes an exact scale-round helper for centered RNS
  product polynomials at the rounded BFV `t/q` boundary, and rounded RNS
  ciphertext multiplication uses that helper for direct product components
  plus a centered two-product sum helper for `c1` cross terms before
  relinearization; product-sum coverage rejects aliasing before
  scale-and-rounding.
- Bounded bootstrap refresh now has direct and registered target-limb
  basis-extension wrappers, and Soracloud bounded Bootstrap execution uses the
  registered wrapper so Add, Multiply, packed RotateLeft, and Bootstrap all stay
  on governed production RNS entry points.

## 2026-06-07 ISO trust rail/policy, fixed-format, and URL host/port redaction hardening

- Hardened `scripts/iso_trust_bundle_verify.py` so trust-bundle `rail` and
  `embedded_signature_policy` values reject secret-looking identifier markers
  before unsupported-rail or unsupported-policy diagnostics run.
- Hardened trust-bundle SHA-256 pins, declared DER digests, and certificate
  policy OIDs so fixed-format trust material rejects secret-looking markers
  before canonical-format diagnostics.
- Hardened `scripts/iso_operator_evidence_verify.py` and
  `scripts/iso_production_readiness.py` so archived trust `rail`,
  `embedded_signature_policy`, and profile-override policy values reject the
  same markers before evidence or readiness summaries can echo or preserve
  forged policy names.
- Hardened evidence/readiness SHA-256 summary fields and receipt metadata so
  archived digest fields reject secret-looking markers before digest-shape
  diagnostics or blockers.
- Normalized ISO URL port parser failures so malformed `--endpoint`,
  `--torii-base-url`, trust source URL, receipt endpoint URL, canary runbook URL,
  evidence URL, and readiness URL diagnostics no longer include the raw parser
  exception text.
- Hardened the same URL surfaces so secret-looking hostname labels are rejected
  before live rail/notary delivery, trust-source ingestion, canary planning,
  receipt verification, evidence archiving, or readiness rollup, and normalized
  non-port URL parser failures to label-only diagnostics.
- Hardened local path, raw CLI, summary-path, artifact-path, and URL-path
  validators with a narrow identifier-style path detector that catches
  composite secret names such as `token-*-secret` and strong key markers without
  preempting legitimate bearer-token file shape checks.
- Added adversarial trust-bundle, evidence-archive, and readiness-rollup
  mutations proving rail, policy, SHA-256, and OID markers are rejected with no
  secret echo.
- Added live rail, notary, and trust-source URL malformed-port cases proving
  secret-looking port strings are not echoed.
- Added trust-source, live rail/notary, canary, receipt, evidence, and readiness
  URL host/parser regressions proving secret-looking host labels and malformed
  parser inputs are rejected without echoing the rejected URL text.
- Added path and URL-path regressions across trust, rail, notary, canary,
  receipt, evidence, readiness, and XSD tooling proving identifier-style secret
  path segments are rejected without echo while ordinary token-file paths still
  reach their intended filesystem validators.
- Hardened receipt verifier metadata replay so raw rail receipts must record
  nullable `profile`/`rail_message_id` keys, digest-bound receipt summaries now
  retain both fields for evidence/readiness replay, omitted optional sidecar
  metadata still matches adapter receipts that record JSON `null`, and source
  sidecars that forge those fields as explicit `null` fail as malformed before
  metadata comparison.
- Hardened raw receipt response metadata so any recorded HTTP response must
  carry a response-body digest/preview pair, response-body digests cannot appear
  without an HTTP status, and failed receipts must preserve a non-secret error
  string even when `--allow-failed` is supplied for local diagnostics.
- Remaining production blockers are still external: live rail/notary delivery
  evidence, official trust/revocation bundles, and redistributable official ISO
  schemas/profile coverage for the remaining gaps.

## 2026-06-07 Kagemusha JVM recursive input Norito guard hardening

- Hardened the Kotlin/JVM and Java Android recursive compact-token prover,
  compact-token verifier, and record-backed recursive aggregation wrappers so
  `recordBundleArchive`, `pallasOpenEnvelopesArchive`, and compact-token
  archives are validated as non-empty Norito archives before owned-copy or
  native dispatch.
- The JVM/Android wrappers now reuse the compact-token archive validation
  corridor for these recursive ABI-7 entry points, keeping malformed local
  archive failures as caller-input errors and preserving recursive compact
  unavailable diagnostics for shape-valid reserved proof-composition state.
- Fixed Java Android identifier normalization to trim only whitespace, mirroring

  non-whitespace control characters; this unblocked the full Java Android test

## 2026-06-07 ISO evidence duplicate diagnostics

- Tightened `scripts/iso_operator_evidence_verify.py` so duplicate embedded
  receipt paths/digests, duplicate compact receipt reuse across canary summaries,
  duplicate trust profile IDs, and duplicate trust bundle digests report only
  field/index labels. The evidence gate no longer appends the repeated
  receipt path, receipt digest, profile id, or bundle digest to these structural
  failures.
- Moved the raw receipt secret-material scan in
  `scripts/iso_operator_receipt_verify.py` ahead of receipt version/kind
  dispatch, so malformed `receipt_kind` values like `token=...` fail label-only
  before unsupported-kind diagnostics can echo them.
- Tightened recursive secret-material scanners in
  `scripts/iso_trust_bundle_verify.py`,
  `scripts/iso_operator_receipt_verify.py`,
  `scripts/iso_operator_evidence_verify.py`, and
  `scripts/iso_production_readiness.py` so forbidden secret-looking field names
  and receipt value secret hits report only the checked path/summary label,
  without appending the rejected key or receipt field name.
- The trust-bundle verifier now also rejects secret-looking identifier-style
  profile IDs, environments, source authority/version strings, DER labels, and
  percent-encoded recursive field names before trust summaries or profile
  overrides can persist them.
- Updated every ISO JSON duplicate-key hook so duplicate object-key diagnostics
  do not echo the repeated key name across rail sidecars, notary anchors/indexes,
  canary runbooks, receipts, trust bundles, XSD manifests/profile catalogs,
  evidence summaries, readiness summaries, embedded receipt-verifier JSON, and
  direct archive receipt-verifier stdout.
- Hardened every ISO unknown-key helper so secret-looking unknown field names
  report only label-level unknown-key failures, while ordinary non-secret
  unknown keys still list the rejected field names for debugging.
- Expanded the shared ISO secret marker vocabulary across raw CLI preflights,
  compact path/value checks, child-output scanners, unknown-key checks, and
  recursive summary scanners so passwords/passphrases, API/access/session keys,
  client secrets, cookies, and Iroha signatures are rejected without echoing the
  rejected material.
- The shared ISO secret scanner now also checks repeated percent-decoded forms,
  so encoded or double-encoded secret-looking key/value material is rejected in
  CLI paths, unknown JSON keys, recursive JSON values, compact evidence/readiness
  paths, and response preview/error redaction paths without echoing the raw or
  decoded secret material. This also closes the canary and XSD `--summary-out`
  path gap for literal and encoded secret-looking path values.
- Shared ISO URL path validators now reject secret-looking key/value material in
  literal, percent-encoded, or double-encoded path segments before live
  rail/notary delivery, canary planning, receipt verification, trust/evidence
  ingestion, or readiness rollup, while reporting only the affected field label.
- The live rail adapter now recursively scans known sidecar fields for
  secret-looking material before unsupported `message_type`, profile,
  `payload_sha256`, or `rail_message_id` diagnostics can echo operator-provided
  values.
- The XSD profile-catalog verifier now recursively scans profile catalog entries
  before field semantics, so secret-looking rail, signature-policy,
  reference-dataset, address-mode, profile-id, or version strings fail
  label-only before value-bearing diagnostics.
- The XSD manifest verifier now rejects secret-looking schema and fixture
  `payload_root` values before schema/fixture namespace or payload-root mismatch
  diagnostics can echo manifest-provided payload names.
- The XSD schema verifier now rejects secret-looking checked-in
  `targetNamespace` attributes before schema namespace mismatch diagnostics can
  echo schema-provided values.
- XSD/XML payload identifiers, schema-root attribute names, and unsupported
  foreign child namespace URIs now also fail with label-only secret-looking
  diagnostics before schema or fixture content can be reflected in stderr.
- The XSD verifier now recursively scans XML fixture element names, namespace
  URIs, attribute names/values, and text/tail content before optional
  `xmllint` validation, and redacts secret-looking `xmllint` failure output
  before composing preflight diagnostics.
- Normalized the secret-looking field-name marker set so hyphenated
  `private-key` and underscore-form `x_iroha_signature` spellings are rejected
  label-only across all ISO unknown-key helpers and recursive scanners. The
  receipt verifier's secret-material pass now also recurses through nested
  receipt JSON objects and arrays before semantic receipt validation.
- Extended adversarial redaction coverage for failed rail/notary remote
  response previews and receipt error strings so upstream password and cookie
  material is redacted in receipts and rejected by the receipt verifier if
  archived unredacted.
- Added adversarial coverage proving those repeated values are absent from
  stderr for embedded receipt-verifier stdout, cross-canary receipt reuse, and
  trust-summary reuse/copy cases, receipt-kind secret-looking values, and
  duplicate secret-looking JSON keys across all ISO entrypoints, plus recursive
  forbidden-field scanner and secret-looking unknown-key coverage for trust,
  receipt, evidence, and readiness paths plus the rail, notary, canary, and XSD
  validators. The same coverage now includes password-style raw CLI tokens,
  unknown JSON fields, recursive fields, receipt values, encoded/double-encoded
  CLI paths, encoded unknown keys, encoded recursive JSON values, and encoded
  response preview/error strings. It also covers literal, encoded, and
  double-encoded secret-looking URL path segments across rail, notary, canary,
  receipt, trust, evidence, and readiness validators; hyphenated `private-key`
  field-name markers, underscore-form Iroha signature field-name markers, and
  nested receipt JSON secret material. The XSD coverage now also proves
  secret-looking checked-in schema `targetNamespace` attributes, manifest or
  schema payload identifiers, fixture payload roots, schema attribute names, and
  foreign-child namespace URIs are rejected without echoing the attribute,
  identifier, or namespace value. Profile-catalog coverage now includes
  identifier-style strings such as profile ids. XML fixture coverage now also
  proves nested fixture content and validator stderr are rejected or redacted
  without echoing secret-looking material. Trust-bundle coverage now includes
  identifier-style summary fields and percent-encoded nested field names.
- The XSD/profile gate state remains unchanged: 11 XML fixtures, 7 checked-in
  schemas, 7 schema-backed XML fixtures validated, 55 profile versions checked,
  31 profile versions schema-backed, 24 profile schema gaps, and 3 restricted
  public schema candidates recorded as blocked source evidence.
- Remaining production blockers are external: live rail/notary evidence,
  official trust/revocation bundles, and redistributable official schemas for
  the remaining payment/securities/collateral profile versions.

- Hardened all ISO operator entrypoints so direct boolean flags reject attached
  `--flag=value` spellings and separate non-option values before argparse can
  echo the supplied value or reinterpret the option. Coverage now spans rail
  gateway, audit notary, operator canary, receipt verification, evidence
  aggregation, production readiness, trust-bundle verification, and XSD fixture
  verification CLIs.
- Updated the ISO engineering backlog and TradFi interop audit notes to record
  the direct boolean-flag preflight alongside the existing path, URL, numeric,
  context, freshness, and raw secret-looking CLI guards. Archived child-command
  evidence now also rejects boolean flags with attached or separate values
  label-only before the rejected value can be echoed.
- The XSD/profile gate state remains unchanged: 11 XML fixtures, 7 checked-in
  schemas, 7 schema-backed XML fixtures validated, 55 profile versions checked,
  31 profile versions schema-backed, 24 profile schema gaps, and 3 restricted
  public schema candidates recorded as blocked source evidence.
- Remaining production blockers are external: live rail/notary evidence,
  official trust/revocation bundles, and redistributable official schemas for
  the remaining payment/securities/collateral profile versions.

## 2026-06-06 Kagemusha Android slot-root link gate

- Rejected symlinked Android device-lab slot directories before scanning or
  signing evidence, so a slot selected by discovery or passed to
  `sign_android_device_lab_evidence.py --slot` cannot be an alias to external
  evidence bytes.
- Preserved caller-provided signer slot paths instead of resolving them before
  validation, allowing the signer helper to detect and reject a symlinked slot
  root before reading `slot.json` or writing signed evidence.

  directories, pinned the guard with

  Android readiness docs and roadmap.

## 2026-06-06 Kagemusha C# archive wrapper copy hardening

- Hardened the C# recursive Kagemusha archive wrappers behind a shared
  `KagemushaNativeArchive` base so constructor inputs and returned
  `NoritoBytes` arrays are validated, size-capped, non-empty Norito V1
  archives and are defensively copied on both write and read.
- Hardened the C# recursive compact verifier wrapper so native verifier bytes
  are accepted only as `0` or `1`; bridge errors and malformed nonzero boolean
  outputs now fail closed instead of being treated as success.
- Hardened the Swift recursive compact native bridge verifier path with the
  same fail-closed `0`/`1` normalization so corrupted C ABI boolean bytes no
  longer coerce to `true`.
- Split Swift recursive compact verifier availability from prover availability
  so verifier-only calls are gated by the verifier symbol/probe instead of the
  prover+allocator surface.
- Split the Kotlin/JVM and Android Java recursive compact verifier availability
  gates the same way: proving still requires the combined prover/verifier
  surface, while verification now uses a verifier-specific native probe.
- Split the JavaScript recursive compact verifier availability gate and public
  export the same way across source, dist, browser stubs, and TypeScript
  declarations so verifier-only native surfaces can verify without requiring
  the prover symbol.
- Hardened the Rust C/JNI, Node host, and Python PyO3 recursive compact
  verifier unavailable classifiers to accept only exact core sentinel strings,
  preventing malformed verifier-key circuit IDs from smuggling the unavailable
  diagnostic through interpolated error text.
- Tightened JavaScript and Python SDK native availability probes so a malformed
  probe is considered rejected only when the error is Kagemusha archive, Norito,
  or probe shaped; vague Kagemusha errors no longer mark compact prover or
  verifier symbols as available.
- Added C# adversarial wrapper tests covering source-array mutation,
  getter-array mutation, null, empty, oversized, malformed, and empty-payload
  Norito inputs for all recursive spend, compact token, recursive aggregation,
  and recursive compact archive wrappers.
- Restored the Swift UC4 payment-token diagnostic test file expected by the
  SDK parity guard, covering malformed UC4 compact marker payloads through
  `decodeText` and wrong canonical compact layout through `decodeNorito`.
- Pinned the new C# archive-copy guard in SDK parity, the PR workflow, and the
  JavaScript parity meta-test so the negative control must stay listed and
  must fail only after injected drift is detected.
- Added Swift parity and JavaScript meta-test pins plus Swift verifier-byte and
  verifier-availability negative controls that prove removal of either guard is
  detected.
- Added JVM/Android parity and JavaScript meta-test pins plus a JVM
  verifier-availability negative control that proves verifier calls cannot drift
  back to the combined prover availability gate.
- Extended the JavaScript recursive compact verifier-surface pins and tests to
  cover verifier-only native availability, browser stubs, package exports, and
  the new TypeScript declaration.
- Added Rust bridge, Node host, and Python PyO3 adversarial verifier
  regressions for Norito-valid compact tokens whose circuit IDs contain the
  unavailable sentinel; malformed tokens now hard-fail instead of returning
  soft invalid results.
- Pinned the exact Rust unavailable classifiers in SDK parity, the PR workflow,
  and the JavaScript parity meta-test with
  `--negative-control-rust-recursive-compact-unavailable-classifier`.
- Added JavaScript and Python adversarial availability tests for vague compact
  prover/verifier probe errors, and pinned the predicate shape with
  `--negative-control-kagemusha-probe-rejection-shape`.

## 2026-06-06 Kagemusha Reserved-lineage proof evidence helper

- Added `scripts/kagemusha_lineage_proof_evidence.py`, a release helper that
  hashes the generated one-hop and append lineage Norito packages, verifier
  records, verifier keys, proving-key archives, and the captured ignored
  record-archive proof log into the strict
  `iroha.kagemusha.lineage_proof_evidence.v1` JSON shape. The helper embeds the
  canonical production ignored-test command, rejects missing artifacts, rejects
  non-finite or non-positive elapsed times, rejects secret-looking local paths,
  requires `--out` to be written directly under `--artifact-dir` so the rollup
  can verify adjacent artifact bytes,
  and refuses commands that set
  `IROHA_KAGEMUSHA_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LINEAGE_KEYGEN` for the production proof run.
- The helper self-validates the generated document with
  `check_lineage_proof_evidence` beside the generated artifact files before
  writing it, so the eventual production-width Reserved-lineage run has an
  executable path from key/proof artifacts to the readiness gate added earlier.
- Added unit coverage for accepted generated evidence plus adversarial missing
  artifact, runtime-keygen command, detached output path, and `NaN`
  elapsed-time cases. The production readiness guard and workflow now include
  `--negative-control-lineage-proof-evidence-helper`.
- This still does not complete production-width keygen/proof. It makes the
  release evidence-generation step executable once the heavyweight proof run
  succeeds.

## 2026-06-06 ISO canary rail trust coverage

- Tightened `scripts/iso_operator_evidence_verify.py` and
  `scripts/iso_production_readiness.py` so every non-legacy `iso-rail-gateway`
  receipt profile exercised by a canary must have matching compact trust
  material for the same profile ID and environment, with same-rail binding for
  built-in rail-named profiles. This blocks forged or stale evidence that swaps
  the trust bundle or profile override ID while keeping successful canary
  receipts.
- Added adversarial evidence/readiness coverage for wrong-rail and wrong
  profile-id trust profiles, plus final-rollup coverage for a same-rail trust
  profile archived under the wrong environment. Custom canonical canary profile
  IDs now have both positive coverage when backed by a matching trust profile
  and negative coverage when the trust material is missing. The evidence gate
  still leaves explicit local `colr.007` diagnostics behind
  `--allow-legacy-colr007`.
- Updated the TradFi audit and engineering backlog to document that final
  readiness rollups and evidence archives bind canary rail receipt profiles to
  compact trust profile coverage.
- Tightened direct receipt archive verification so digest-correct canary
  receipt summaries cannot relabel archived receipt artifacts under a different
  `*.receipt.json` filename. The evidence gate fails closed on the relabel, and
  the final readiness rollup emits `evidence.archive_receipt_canary_path_mismatch`.
- Tightened `scripts/iso_operator_receipt_verify.py` so rail receipts that omit
  an explicit profile now require `--allow-default-profile`, and the receipt
  verifier emits `allow_default_profile` in its digest-bound summary. The
  canary, evidence, and readiness gates replay that flag explicitly, and the
  checked-in operator canary templates now set `verify.allow_default_profile=false`
  under `--require-explicit-policy`.
- Versioned receipt-verifier summaries with `version=1` and made evidence and
  readiness gates fail closed on missing or unsupported receipt-summary
  versions. This keeps archived canary and direct receipt evidence tied to the
  schema the verifier actually emitted.
- Versioned XSD fixture summaries with `version=1` and tightened readiness so
  aggregate evidence summary versions must be exact non-boolean integers. XSD
  version drift is now surfaced as `xsd.summary_version_unsupported` in the
  final readiness blockers.
- Versioned operator canary and trust-bundle summaries with `version=1`. The
  evidence gate now rejects missing, boolean, or unsupported canary/trust
  summary versions before archiving, and readiness reports compact rollup
  version drift with `evidence.canary_summary_version_unsupported` or
  `trust.summary_version_unsupported`.
- Tightened remaining ISO input version checks so XSD manifests, trust bundles,
  notary audit indexes, notary anchors, persisted record sources, and adapter
  receipts require exact integer version values rather than accepting JSON
  boolean `true`. Receipt `status_code` metadata now rejects JSON booleans before
  status-success policy evaluation. Notary audit-index, anchor, and receipt
  `record_count` fields also reject JSON booleans instead of relying on Python's
  `True == 1` equality behavior. Canary, evidence, and XSD child-process output
  byte caps reject boolean aliases at their internal bounded-command entry
  points, and the canary runner rejects boolean `--output-limit-bytes` values
  before plan-only summaries can be emitted.
- Hardened the ISO regular-file readers in the rail gateway, audit notary,
  receipt verifier, canary runner, evidence verifier, readiness rollup,
  trust-bundle verifier, and XSD fixture verifier so `max_bytes=True` or other
  non-integer aliases fail before filesystem metadata is inspected. The rail
  gateway payload `_bounded_read` now applies the same exact positive-integer
  policy.
- Tightened archived canary child-command validation in
  `scripts/iso_operator_evidence_verify.py` so value-taking flags fail closed
  when their separate or equals-form value is empty or another `--flag` token.
  This covers URL, bearer-token, artifact path, XML path, receipt path, integer,
  and timeout flags before production evidence can archive ambiguous command
  lines.
- Tightened direct ISO CLI path preflights across the rail gateway, audit
  notary, receipt verifier, canary runner, evidence verifier, readiness rollup,
  trust-bundle verifier, and XSD fixture verifier so bare path flags, empty
  separate values, empty equals-form values, and flag-looking separate or
  equals-form path values are rejected as missing path values before any local
  file or network work starts. The rail gateway now also applies the same direct
  path preflight to explicit `--message` XML paths before sidecar or payload reads.
  The live rail-gateway and audit-notary adapters
  also reject secret-looking key/value material in local paths before those
  paths can be persisted into receipts, reject missing, empty, or flag-looking
  `--torii-base-url`/`--endpoint` URL values before argparse parsing, and audit-notary
  anchor `store_dir` paths reject the same material before record-source
  verification. Rail-gateway, audit-notary, canary, evidence, readiness, and
  XSD numeric CLI preflights now reject malformed, empty, flag-looking, or
  secret-looking numeric values before argparse can echo operator-provided
  input. All ISO operator entry points now also reject secret-looking raw CLI
  tokens before argparse can echo unknown arguments. Evidence and
  production-readiness provider/environment context flags reject missing, empty,
  or flag-looking values before argparse or summary loading. Trust-bundle
  `--max-source-age-days` rejects missing, empty, flag-looking, malformed, or
  secret-looking freshness budgets before argparse or bundle reads.
- Sanitized remaining ISO duplicate diagnostics for audit records, receipt
  archive records, profile-catalog string lists and amount units, trust-bundle
  SHA/OID/DER material, evidence receipt kinds and duplicate summary digests,
  readiness compact-summary digests, and rail-gateway duplicate payload or
  rail-message-id checks so they report only field/index labels instead of
  echoing rejected duplicate values.
- Rail-gateway and audit-notary bearer-token file read/decode/size failures now
  report the credential input label instead of echoing runtime token file paths.
- `scripts/iso_xsd_fixture_verify.py --require-profile-schema-backed-versions`
  now uses the default `DEFAULT_PROFILES_JSON` catalog when `--profile-catalog`
  is omitted, so the direct release gate fails on current profile-advertised
  schema gaps instead of requiring a redundant catalog path argument.
